Compared with conventional laser, subthreshold laser probably yields similar improvements in visual acuity and reduces retinal pigment epithelium damage but probably leads to a lower rate of subretinal fluid resolution. When compared with observation, subthreshold laser may result in similar visual acuity outcomes but may reduce persistent metamorphopsia and increase subretinal fluid resolution, although the certainty of evidence is very low. Compared with half-dose photodynamic therapy, subthreshold laser may provide comparable visual outcomes but lower anatomical improvement, with very low certainty of evidence.

Conclusion

In acute CSC, subthreshold laser appears safer than conventional laser and produces similar visual outcomes, although its anatomical efficacy is limited. Its potential advantages over observation or photodynamic therapy remain uncertain because of low-certainty evidence.

records.title: A CONSENSUS ON RISK MITIGATION FOR BROLUCIZUMAB IN NEOVASCULAR AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION: Patient Selection, Evaluation, and Treatment.

content.title: A CONSENSUS ON RISK MITIGATION FOR BROLUCIZUMAB IN NEOVASCULAR AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION: Patient Selection, Evaluation, and Treatment.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Brolucizumab has high efficacy in retinal fluid resolution and provides the possibility for longer dosing intervals in the treatment of neovascular age-related macular degeneration. However, brolucizumab has been associated with events of retinal vasculitis and retinal vascular occlusion typically in the presence of other signs of intraocular inflammation (IOI). The purpose of this report is to provide guidance on the use of brolucizumab for neovascular age-related macular degeneration to a global audience.

Methods

A literature review was conducted on adverse events related to IOI after administration of brolucizumab in eyes with neovascular age-related macular degeneration.

Results

Possible risk factors for IOI and retinal vascular occlusion after brolucizumab should be considered before administering brolucizumab. Patients who receive brolucizumab should be educated on the symptoms, signs, and time course of IOI after brolucizumab. Before each injection of brolucizumab, physicians should assess the eye for any signs of inflammation and not treat with brolucizumab if inflammation is detected. Treatment of IOI should be prompt and provided with particular attention to the posterior segment.

Conclusion

Careful patient selection, patient education, assessment for inflammation, and intensive treatment of possible inflammation are important when using brolucizumab in patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration.

records.title: A Network Meta-Analysis of Retreatment Rates following Bevacizumab, Ranibizumab, Aflibercept, and Laser for Retinopathy of Prematurity.

content.title: A Network Meta-Analysis of Retreatment Rates following Bevacizumab, Ranibizumab, Aflibercept, and Laser for Retinopathy of Prematurity.
content.abstract:
Topic

To compare bevacizumab, ranibizumab, aflibercept, and laser treatment as primary therapies for retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) in terms of retreatment rate.

Clinical relevance

Anti-VEGF agents are increasingly used as primary treatment for ROP and may provide superior outcomes compared with laser in posterior disease. Head-to-head comparisons between different anti-VEGFs are lacking.

Methods

We searched CENTRAL, Embase, MEDLINE, and CINAHL databases for randomized controlled trials and nonrandomized comparative studies that had been reported as of March 2022. We included studies that used bevacizumab, ranibizumab, aflibercept or laser for ROP with comparable cohorts and treatment criteria. Studies were evaluated by the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation framework, and those with biased case selection, nonrandomized case-control, or lack of control group were excluded. Frequentist meta-analyses of proportions determined the absolute primary retreatment rate of each modality and Bayesian network meta-analyses compared pairs of treatments in type 1 and Zone I ROP.

Results

In all, 30 studies (4686 eyes) were included in the network meta-analyses. For type 1 ROP, single-treatment success rates (i.e., likelihood of needing no further treatment) were 89.3% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 83.8%-93.8%; n = 1552) for laser, 87.0% (95% CI: 78.6%-93.8%; n = 2081) for bevacizumab, 80.7% (95% CI: 62.0%-94.4%; n = 326) for aflibercept, and 74.0% (95% CI: 62.7%-84.1%; n = 727) for ranibizumab. Bayesian network meta-analysis indicates that laser treatment is associated with a significant 62% (95% credible interval [CrI]: 16%-83%) reduction in retreatment risk compared with ranibizumab, while no significant difference was found among other pairwise comparisons. The mean ± standard error of the mean times to secondary treatment following primary aflibercept (12.96 ± 0.47 weeks) and bevacizumab (11.36 ± 0.54 weeks) therapy were significantly longer than that for primary ranibizumab (9.29 ± 0.43weeks) therapy (P = 7 × 10-7 and P = 9 × 10-3, respectively). For Zone I ROP, single-treatment success rates were 91.2% (95% CI: 83.6-96.9; n = 231) for bevacizumab, 78.3% (95% CI: 61.4-91.9; n = 100) for ranibizumab, and 65.9% (95% CI: 41.4-87.2; n = 158) for laser treatment. In this case, Bayesian network meta-analysis suggests that primary bevacizumab is associated with a significant 67% (95% CrI:10%-90%) reduction in retreatment risk compared with laser treatment.

Conclusions

Laser was associated with a lower rate of retreatment than ranibizumab in type 1 ROP (Zones I and II combined), while bevacizumab was associated with a lower rate of retreatment than laser in Zone I ROP. Aflibercept and bevacizumab demonstrate longer duration of action than ranibizumab for ROP.

records.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence-Based Automated Diabetic Retinopathy Screening in Real-World Settings: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence-Based Automated Diabetic Retinopathy Screening in Real-World Settings: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence (AI)-based automated diabetic retinopathy (DR) screening in real-world settings.

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis METHODS: We conducted a systematic review of relevant literature from January 2012 to August 2022 using databases including PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science. The quality of studies was evaluated using Quality Assessment for Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2 (QUADAS-2) checklist. We calculated pooled accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and diagnostic odds ratio (DOR) as summary measures. The study protocol was registered with the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO - CRD42022367034).

Results

We included 34 studies which utilized AI algorithms for diagnosing DR based on real-world fundus images. Quality assessment of these studies indicated a low risk of bias and low applicability concern. Among gradable images, the overall pooled accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and DOR were 81%, 94% (95% CI: 92.0-96.0), 89% (95% CI: 85.0-92.0) and 128 (95% CI: 80-204) respectively. Sub-group analysis showed that, when acceptable quality imaging could be obtained, non-mydriatic fundus images had a better DOR of 143 (95% CI: 82-251) and studies using 2 field images had a better DOR of 161 (95% CI 74-347). Our meta-regression analysis revealed a statistically significant association between DOR and variables such as the income status, and the type of fundus camera.

Conclusion

Our findings indicate that AI algorithms have acceptable performance in screening for DR using fundus images compared to human graders. Implementing a fundus camera with AI-based software has the potential to assist ophthalmologists in reducing their workload and improving the accuracy of DR diagnosis.

records.title: Risk of Subsequent Dementia or Alzheimer Disease Among Patients With Age-Related Macular Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

content.title: Risk of Subsequent Dementia or Alzheimer Disease Among Patients With Age-Related Macular Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Alzheimer disease (AD), a common form of dementia, shares several clinical and pathologic features with age-related macular degeneration (AMD). Epidemiologic reports on the association of AMD with subsequent dementia or AD are inconsistent.

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis.

Methods

The Meta-analysis of Observational Studies in Epidemiology reporting guidelines were applied. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale was used to evaluate the risk of bias in the included cohort studies that examined the association of AMD with subsequent dementia or AD. We estimated the pooled hazard ratios (HRs) of dementia or AD using random effects model meta-analysis and subgroup analysis on different follow-up periods, AMD subtype, gender, age, study design, and methods to ascertain dementia or AD.

Results

A total of 8 223 581 participants were included in 8 studies published during 2000-2021. The meta-analysis showed that AMD was significantly associated with subsequent dementia (pooled HR 1.22, 95% CI 1.01-1.47) or AD (pooled HR 1.21, 95% CI 1.03-1.43). Our secondary analysis revealed that the association was more noticeable in dry AMD than wet AMD.

Conclusions

Patients with AMD have higher risks of developing dementia or AD, and therefore identifying related comorbidities and retinal biomarkers is much warranted for older adults with AMD in ophthalmologic practice.

records.title: The physiology of dark adaptation: Progress and future directions.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: The physiology of dark adaptation: Progress and future directions.
content.abstract: Exposure of the eye to bright bleaching light produces a large decrease in photoreceptor sensitivity, followed by a slow return during adaptation to darkness. Although much progress has been made understanding the nature of this phenomenon, particularly its biochemistry, less is known about the physiology of dark adaptation. In this review, we summarize the evidence for desensitization produced by photoproducts of bleaching, especially apo-opsin, that is opsin without bound chromophore. We describe the relationship between these studies and diseases such as vitamin A deprivation and congenital stationary night blindness; the effects of analogs of chromophore on photoreceptor sensitivity; and the roles of transducin, rhodopsin kinase, and arrestin. We review many specialized features of dark adaptation in cones, including the role of retinal G protein-coupled receptor (RGR) opsin. For both rod and cone dark adaptation, we summarize some of the principal uncertainties in our understanding. We hope our review will provide a guide to past work as well as an indicator of many possible areas of future research.

records.title: Global Estimates of Diabetic Retinopathy Prevalence and Progression in Pregnant Women With Preexisting Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

content.title: Global Estimates of Diabetic Retinopathy Prevalence and Progression in Pregnant Women With Preexisting Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Importance

Diabetic retinopathy (DR) may be worsened by pregnancy in pregnant women with preexisting type 1 diabetes (T1D) or type 2 diabetes (T2D). Conflicting findings from previous studies have resulted in inconsistencies in guidelines regarding DR management in pregnancy. Global estimates of DR prevalence and progression in pregnancy are therefore required to provide clearer information about the overall true burden of DR in this population.

Objective

To estimate the prevalence of DR and its progression rate in pregnant women with preexisting T1D or T2D diagnosed before pregnancy.

Data sources

For this systematic review and meta-analysis, conducted from November 27, 2018, to June 29, 2021, a systematic literature search was conducted in MEDLINE/Ovid, Embase/Ovid, and Scopus databases to identify English-language articles that were published from inception through October 2020.

Study selection

Observational studies that reported on DR and its changes in pregnant women with preexisting T1D and T2D.

Data extraction and synthesis

Two independent reviewers extracted relevant data from each included study. Data were pooled using a random-effects model with the Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation. This study followed the Meta-analysis of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (MOOSE) reporting guidelines.

Main outcomes and measures

Prevalence of any DR, proliferative DR (PDR), and DR progression rates.

Results

A total of 18 observational studies involving 1464 pregnant women with T1D and 262 pregnant women with T2D were included in the analysis. The pooled prevalence of any DR and PDR in early pregnancy was 52.3 (95% CI, 41.9-62.6) and 6.1 (95% CI, 3.1-9.8) per 100 pregnancies, respectively. The pooled progression rate per 100 pregnancies for new DR development was 15.0 (95% CI, 9.9-20.8), worsened nonproliferative DR was 31.0 (95% CI, 23.2-39.2), progression from nonproliferative DR to PDR was 6.3 (95% CI, 3.3-10.0), and worsened PDR was 37.0 (95% CI, 21.2-54.0). DR progression rates per 100 pregnancies were similar between the T1D and T2D groups, except for the development of new DR (T1D groups: 15.8; 95% CI, 10.5-21.9; T2D groups: 9.0; 95% CI, 4.9-14.8). A global trend toward a lower DR progression rate was observed after the 1989 St Vincent Declaration.

Conclusions and relevance

Results of this systematic review and meta-analysis suggest that women with T1D and T2D had a similar risk of DR progression during pregnancy. Despite improvements in the management of diabetes and diabetes during pregnancy, DR prevalence and progression in pregnant women with diabetes remains higher than the nonpregnant population with diabetes, highlighting the need to improve DR management in pregnancy.

records.title: The versatile roles of retinal pigment epithelium in the pathophysiology of retinitis pigmentosa.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: The versatile roles of retinal pigment epithelium in the pathophysiology of retinitis pigmentosa.
content.abstract: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is a group of hereditary retinal diseases that lead to progressive vision loss, with most disease-causing genes expressed in rod photoreceptors and a smaller fraction in retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) cells. The RPE and photoreceptor cells share a symbiotic relationship characterized by close spatial and functional interactions that play a pivotal role in vision. Although the role of RPE is fundamental to the retina, its involvement in retinal pathogenesis, and, in particular, in RP remains underappreciated. In this review, we summarize morphological alterations in the RPE resulting from pathogenic mutations specific to RPE cells, as well as those occurring secondary to photoreceptor degeneration. We provide a comprehensive summary of how mutations in RPE-specific genes play a key role in the pathophysiology of RP. Finally, we discuss the latest therapeutic approaches, including AAV-mediated gene augmentation, RPE cell transplantation, and pharmacological interventions.

records.title: IMPACT OF FLUID COMPARTMENTS ON FUNCTIONAL OUTCOMES FOR PATIENTS WITH NEOVASCULAR AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION: A Systematic Literature Review.

content.title: IMPACT OF FLUID COMPARTMENTS ON FUNCTIONAL OUTCOMES FOR PATIENTS WITH NEOVASCULAR AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION: A Systematic Literature Review.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Understanding the impact of fluid in different retinal compartments is critical to developing treatment paradigms that optimize visual acuity and reduce treatment burden in neovascular age-related macular degeneration. This systematic review aimed to determine the impact of persistent/new subretinal fluid, intraretinal fluid, and subretinal pigment epithelial fluid on visual acuity over 1 year of treatment.

Methods

Publication eligibility and data extraction were conducted according to Cochrane methods: 27 of the 1,797 screened records were eligible.

Results

Intraretinal fluid negatively affected visual acuity at baseline and throughout treatment, with foveal intraretinal fluid associated with lower visual acuity than extrafoveal intraretinal fluid. Some studies found that subretinal fluid (particularly subfoveal) was associated with higher visual acuity at Year 1 and longer term, and others suggested subretinal fluid did not affect visual acuity at Years 1 and 2. Data on the effects of subretinal pigment epithelial fluid were scarce, and consensus was not reached. Few studies reported numbers of injections associated with fluid status.

Conclusion

To optimally manage neovascular age-related macular degeneration, clinicians should understand the impact of fluid compartments on visual acuity. After initial treatment, antivascular endothelial growth factor regimens that tolerate stable subretinal fluid (if visual acuity is stable/improved) but not intraretinal fluid may enable patients to achieve their best possible visual acuity. Confirmatory studies are required to validate these findings.

records.title: Pathological mechanism in Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy and myotonic dystrophy type 1: more than meets the eye.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Pathological mechanism in Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy and myotonic dystrophy type 1: more than meets the eye.
content.abstract: Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy (FECD) is a heritable disorder distinguished by a progressive degeneration of the corneal endothelium. In its late-onset form, FECD has been associated with a trinucleotide repeat (TNR) expansion (CTG18.1) located in an intronic region of the TCF4 gene, whose frequency is variable among different ancestry groups. Since its discovery, studies investigating CTG18.1-mediated pathogenesis have steadily increased, yet much concerning the unique and tissue-specific clinical features of the disease, as well as its heritable mode of transmission, remain poorly understood. The field of repeat expansion disorders has greatly informed mechanistic understanding of CTG18.1-mediated FECD. In particular, molecular mechanisms underlying myotonic dystrophy type 1, attributed to a CTG expansion in the 3' UTR of the DMPK gene, have considerably informed the FECD field, despite its stark contrast in terms of multisystemic manifestations and variable age at onset. In this work, we critically discuss the non-mutually shared pathogenic parallelisms existing between the pathologies, as well as the unique molecular signatures exhibited by FECD and DM1, speculating on potential research directions for future investigations. Moreover, we discuss the few studies published over the past decade describing the occurrence of FECD in DM1 patients. Here, we debate possible shared molecular signatures that could explain FECD development as a consequence of a non-coding CTG expansion, irrespective of loci (e.g. DMPK or TCF4), and discuss experimental approaches to explain whether these pathologies share toxic mechanisms that arise from these distinct repeat elements.

records.title: Investing in vision: Innovation in retinal therapeutics and the influence on venture capital investment.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Investing in vision: Innovation in retinal therapeutics and the influence on venture capital investment.
content.abstract: Since the groundbreaking approval of the first anti-VEGF therapy in 2004, the retinal therapeutics field has undergone a remarkable transformation, witnessing a surge in novel, disease-modifying therapeutics for a broad spectrum of retinal diseases, extending beyond exudative VEGF-driven conditions. The surge in scientific advancement and the pressing, unmet, medical need have captured the attention of venture capital investors, who have collectively invested close to $10 billion in research and development of new retinal therapeutics between 2004 and 2023. Notably, the field of exudative diseases has gradually shifted away from trying to outcompete anti-VEGF therapeutics towards lowering the overall treatment burden by reducing injection frequency. Simultaneously, a new era has emerged in the non-exudative field, targeting prevalent conditions like dry AMD and rare indications such as Retinitis pigmentosa. This has led to promising drug candidates in development, culminating in the landmark approval of Luxturna for a rare form of Retinitis pigmentosa. The validation of new mechanisms, such as the complement pathway in dry AMD has paved the way for the approvals of Syvovre (Apellis) and Izervay (Iveric/Astellas), marking the first two therapies for this condition. In this comprehensive review, we share our view on the cumulative lessons from the past two decades in developing retinal therapeutics, covering both positive achievements and challenges. We also contextualize the investments, strategic partnering deals, and acquisitions of biotech companies, pharmaceutical companies venture capital investors in retinal therapeutics, respectively. Finally, we provide an outlook and potentially a forward-looking roadmap on novel retinal therapeutics, highlighting the emergence of potential new intervention strategies, such as cell-based therapies, gene editing, and combination therapies. We conclude that upcoming developments have the potential to further stimulate venture capital investments, which ultimately could facilitate the development and delivery of new therapies to patients in need.

records.title: Shining light on CRISPR/Cas9 therapeutics for inherited retinal diseases.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Shining light on CRISPR/Cas9 therapeutics for inherited retinal diseases.
content.abstract: Inherited retinal diseases (IRDs), such as retinitis pigmentosa, are a heterogenous group of genetic eye diseases characterized by degeneration of photoreceptors. They are the leading cause of blindness in the working age population in high-income countries and are an ideal target for the expanding gene editing tool kit, including rapidly evolving CRISPR/Cas9 technology. In this review, we provide a comprehensive analysis of CRISPR/Cas9 technologies currently being explored as therapeutic interventions for IRDs. Given the challenges posed by the growing complexity and size of gene editing systems, the delivery of these therapeutics to the retina has necessitated innovative approaches. We review current delivery methods, including nanoparticles, virus-like particles and traditional viral vectors, highlighting their advantages and limitations. This review underscores the potential transformative impact of gene editing on genetic disease management, emphasising that advancements in these technologies, coupled with improved pre-clinical models, bring clinically safe and effective treatments for IRDs within view.

records.title: Effectiveness of Conventional Digital Fundus Photography-Based Teleretinal Screening for Diabetic Retinopathy and Diabetic Macular Edema: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology.

content.title: Effectiveness of Conventional Digital Fundus Photography-Based Teleretinal Screening for Diabetic Retinopathy and Diabetic Macular Edema: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology.
content.abstract:
Purpose

This American Academy of Ophthalmology Ophthalmic Technology Assessment aims to assess the effectiveness of conventional teleretinal screening (TS) in detecting diabetic retinopathy (DR) and diabetic macular edema (DME).

Methods

A literature search of the PubMed database was conducted most recently in July 2023 to identify data published between 2006 and 2023 on any of the following elements related to TS effectiveness: (1) the accuracy of TS in detecting DR or DME compared with traditional ophthalmic screening with dilated fundus examination or 7-standard field Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study photography, (2) the impact of TS on DR screening compliance rates or other patient behaviors, and (3) cost-effectiveness and patient satisfaction of TS compared with traditional DR screening. Identified studies then were rated based on the Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine grading system.

Results

Eight level I studies, 14 level II studies, and 2 level III studies were identified in total. Although cross-study comparison is challenging because of differences in reference standards and grading methods, TS demonstrated acceptable sensitivity and good specificity in detecting DR; moderate to good agreement between TS and reference-standard DR grading was observed. Performance of TS was not as robust in detecting DME, although the number of studies evaluating DME specifically was limited. Two level I studies, 5 level II studies, and 1 level III study supported that TS had a positive impact on overall DR screening compliance, even increasing it by more than 2-fold in one study. Studies assessing cost-effectiveness and patient satisfaction were not graded formally, but they generally showed that TS was cost-effective and preferred by patients over traditional surveillance.

Conclusions

Conventional TS is an effective approach to DR screening not only for its accuracy in detecting referable-level disease, but also for improving screening compliance in a cost-effective manner that may be preferred by patients. Further research is needed to elucidate the ideal approach of TS that may involve integration of artificial intelligence or other imaging technologies in the future.

Financial disclosure(s)

Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found in the Footnotes and Disclosures at the end of this article.

records.title: Impact of the Time to Surgery on Visual Outcomes for Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment Repair: A Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Impact of the Time to Surgery on Visual Outcomes for Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment Repair: A Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To determine the relationship between time from symptom onset or presentation to repair and visual outcomes for macula-on and macula-off rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD).

Design

Meta-analysis.

Methods

We searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane Library for randomized controlled trials and observational studies comparing best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) based on time to RRD repair. Study identifiers, baseline characteristics, intervention characteristics, and visual outcomes were extracted. We conducted a random effects meta-analysis. Sensitivity analyses included leave-1-out and influence analyses. Primary outcomes included mean difference (MD) in final BCVA, MD between preoperative and final BCVA (∆BCVA), and relative risk of final BCVA <0.4 logMAR for macula-off RRD repair in 0-3 vs 4-7 days and macula-on RRD repair in 0-24 vs >24 hours. Secondary outcomes assessed other time points.

Results

Twenty observational studies reported on 1929 patients. Macula-off RRD repair in 0-3 days from symptom onset was superior to 4-7 days for final BCVA (MD -0.06 [95% CI -0.09, -0.03], P < .001) but was not different for ∆BCVA (P > .05). Macula-on repair in 0-24 hours from presentation was superior to >24 hours for final BCVA (MD -0.02 [95% CI -0.03, -0.01], P < .05) but was not different for ∆BCVA (P > .05).

Conclusions

Macula-off RRD repair in 0-3 days from symptom onset may have better final BCVA compared to repair in 4-7 days. Macula-on RRD repair in 0-24 hours of presentation may have better final BCVA compared to repair in >24 hours. These results were supported by moderate- and low-quality evidence, respectively, and may have been influenced by differences in baseline BCVA.

records.title: Unravelling CYP4V2: Clinical features, genetic insights, pathogenic mechanisms and therapeutic strategies in Bietti crystalline corneoretinal dystrophy.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Unravelling CYP4V2: Clinical features, genetic insights, pathogenic mechanisms and therapeutic strategies in Bietti crystalline corneoretinal dystrophy.
content.abstract: Inherited retinal dystrophies (IRDs) comprise a spectrum of disease phenotypes with genetic heterogeneity and clinical phenotypic diversity. Bietti crystalline corneoretinal dystrophy (BCD) represents a distinct IRD subtype characterized by crystalline deposits in the retina. Although rare in Western populations, BCD ranks among the most prevalent IRDs in East Asia, affecting an estimated 124,000 to 377,000 individuals worldwide. As a severe type of IRD, BCD demonstrates accelerated progression and currently lacks effective treatment. The BCD disease is caused by a biallelic mutation in the CYP4V2 gene. With a coding sequence (CDS) of 1,578 bp, CYP4V2 can be effectively encapsulated into adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors. As a hydroxylase, CYP4V2 is mainly expressed in retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) cells, which can be transduced by AAVs and are suitable for gene augmentation therapy that replaces the function of mutant proteins. Given the large patient population, severe visual impairment, and feasibility of gene therapy, several research groups are interested in developing gene therapy products for BCD, and two products entering Phase III clinical trials have made significant progress. This review outlines the clinical features, genetic insights and pathogenic mechanisms of BCD and discusses the ongoing gene therapy clinical trials, including efficacy and concerns. This knowledge will help us bridge the gap between molecular studies and clinical treatments, facilitating translation from bench to bedside. We believe that advancements in BCD gene therapy will inform the treatment of other IRDs.

records.title: Understanding glaucoma as astrocyte-driven neurodegeneration in the optic nerve head: an integrative clinicopathological perspective.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Understanding glaucoma as astrocyte-driven neurodegeneration in the optic nerve head: an integrative clinicopathological perspective.
content.abstract: Glaucoma is characterized by the progressive loss of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), primarily driven by axonal degeneration within the optic nerve head (ONH). Recent advances in neurodegeneration and neuroinflammation research have opened new astrocyte-centered perspectives on glaucoma pathogenesis. Critical evaluation of emerging evidence suggests that ONH astrocyte changes may serve as the primary driver of pathogenesis, with loss of astrocytic support playing a substantial role. Evidence from experimental glaucoma models reveals that early intraocular pressure (IOP)-induced remodeling of the ONH astrocyte network precedes RGC axonal damage, potentially mediated by impaired astrocytic control of electrophysiological homeostasis within the surrounding extracellular space. Furthermore, the heterogeneous glia-neuron ratio (GNR) across the normal human ONH lamina cribrosa exhibits an inverse topographic association with the spatiotemporal pattern of regional vulnerability observed clinically in glaucoma, suggesting that regional variations in the astrocyte-to-neuron ratio, reflecting astrocytic support reserve, may critically determine local tissue susceptibility to glaucomatous stress. Recent optical coherence tomography-based insights into the regional vulnerability in human glaucoma are discussed. This clinicopathological interpretation may offer a comprehensive framework that coherently integrates diverse neurodegenerative mechanisms into a unified clinical entity, bridge the conventional mechanical and ischemic theories of glaucoma by highlighting astrocyte changes as a common primary target of risk factors, and ultimately redefine glaucoma as astrocyte-driven neurodegeneration in the biomechanically and bioenergetically vulnerable ONH.

records.title: Influence of capsular tension ring implantation on dynamic in vivo capsular apposition and intraocular lens behavior in highly myopic eyes.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Influence of capsular tension ring implantation on dynamic in vivo capsular apposition and intraocular lens behavior in highly myopic eyes.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the dynamic in vivo capsular apposition to the intraocular lens (IOL) in highly myopic eyes after capsular tension ring (CTR) implantation using swept-source optical coherence tomography (SS-OCT), and to investigate its correlation with in-the-bag IOL behavior.

Setting

Eye Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University, Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, China.

Design

Prospective randomized clinical trial.

Methods

Highly myopic patients undergoing cataract surgery were randomized to receive CTR implantation or not. SS-OCT was performed at 1 day, 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months to assess capsular apposition. Postoperative aqueous depth (PAD), IOL rotation, and anterior and posterior capsular opacification (ACO/PCO) were evaluated at each follow-up visit.

Results

A total of 29 eyes with CTR implantation and 30 eyes without CTR were included. The CTR group exhibited accelerated anterior capsular apposition, demonstrated by a smaller lens-anterior capsule distance (LCD) at 1 day and a higher proportion of anterior capsular apposition at 1 week. From 1 month onward, posterior capsular apposition occurred more frequently in the CTR group. At 1 day, the average LCD positively correlated with both PAD and IOL rotation. During subsequent follow-up period, the mean capsular bend index exhibited negative correlations with the absolute changes in PAD and IOL rotational speed. The CTR group developed less severe ACO, eyes with incomplete posterior capsular apposition had a higher risk of PCO.

Conclusions

CTR implantation facilitates accelerated anterior and more complete posterior capsular apposition to the IOL in highly myopic eyes, which may contribute to improved postoperative IOL stability and a reduced incidence of capsular opacification.

records.title: Comparison of the Moussa Intraocular Lens Formula to contemporary formulas in a multicenter study.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Comparison of the Moussa Intraocular Lens Formula to contemporary formulas in a multicenter study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the refractive predictive accuracy of the Moussa intraocular lens (IOL) formula compared with Kane, EVO, PEARL-DGS, K6, Hoffer-QST, and Barrett Universal II (BUII).

Setting

Birmingham Midland Eye Centre (Birmingham), Manchester Royal Eye Hospital and Newmedica (Manchester), UK.

Design

Multicenter, retrospective, consecutive, nonrandomized observational case series (September 2022-June 2025).

Methods

Included were one eye per patient undergoing uncomplicated phacoemulsification. Preoperative biometry used the IOLMaster 700, Lenstar LS900, or Pentacam AXL Wave. Lens-constants were optimized to zero mean prediction error (PE) for each formula and lens-biometer combination. Primary outcome was mean absolute error (MAE), evaluated using heteroscedastic studentized bootstrap analysis (2000 iterations; Holm correction). Secondary outcomes included median absolute error, root-mean-square error, standard deviation of PE, and proportions of eyes within ±0.25diopter (D) and ±0.50D.

Results

Included were 2550 patients (2550 eyes; mean age 74.0±10.0 years; 1068 male patients [41.9%]). Moussa produced a lower MAE (0.348 D) than Kane (0.359D), EVO (0.363D), PEARL-DGS (0.367D), K6 (0.367D), Hoffer-QST (0.377D), and BUII (0.379D; all p<.001). In short eyes (≤22.0mm), Moussa (0.412D) demonstrated lower error than K6 (p<.001), BUII (p<.001), Hoffer-QST (p=.008), EVO (p=.008), PEARL-DGS (p=.014), and Kane (p=.039). In long eyes (≥26.0 mm), Moussa (0.342 D) had lower error than Kane, BUII, Hoffer-QST (all p<.001), and K6 (p=.045), but not EVO (p=.068) or PEARL-DGS (p=.202).

Conclusions

The Moussa formula demonstrated high predictive accuracy across multiple biometry platforms, with statistically lower overall MAE than the comparator formulas. Absolute differences from the closest-performing formulas were modest, and ±0.50D outcomes were similar to Kane and EVO. These findings support Moussa as a clinically relevant contemporary option for IOL power calculation, with encouraging results in short and long eyes requiring further targeted validation.

records.title: Do hyperopic eyes have narrower iridocorneal angles than myopic eyes at the same anterior chamber depth? A matched study.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Do hyperopic eyes have narrower iridocorneal angles than myopic eyes at the same anterior chamber depth? A matched study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare iridocorneal angle (ICA) and other anterior segment anatomical parameters between hyperopic and myopic eyes with the same anterior chamber depth (ACD), which could have important implications for hyperopic posterior chamber phakic intraocular lens (PC-pIOL) implantation.

Setting

Private eye hospital.

Design

Retrospective observational study.

Methods

ACD, ICA, anterior chamber volume (ACV), white-to-white (WTW), and spherical equivalent were obtained from records of patients aged 21-55 and analysed using paired and regression approaches. Hyperopic and myopic eyes were matched 1:1 by ACD and compared with paired t-tests. Analysis of covariance was performed with ICA as the dependent variable, refractive group as the fixed factor and ACD as a covariate. An ICA ≥ 35 degrees was defined as a sufficiently wide angle.

Results

Forty-four hyperopic and 72 myopic eyes were included. In the paired analysis, ICA and ACV did not differ significantly between groups (p = 0.356 and 0.446 respectively). In the regression analysis, refractive group was not a significant predictor of ICA after adjustment for ACD (p = 0.193). The proportion of eyes with wide ICA increased with ACD but did not differ between groups.

Conclusion

We found no statistically significant anatomical difference in Scheimpflug-measured ICA and ACV between hyperopic and myopic eyes with the same ACD in this population. Nevertheless, the current thicker hyperopic lens design without a central hole remains an important reason for exercising greater caution with hyperopic PC-pIOL implantation.

records.title: Clinical outcomes according to the functional classification of intraocular lenses based on depth-of-field after myopic Laser in situ Keratomileusis.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Clinical outcomes according to the functional classification of intraocular lenses based on depth-of-field after myopic Laser in situ Keratomileusis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare refractive predictability and functional visual outcomes among three depth-of-field (DOFi)-based intraocular lens (IOL) categories in eyes with previous myopic laser in situ keratomileusis (LASIK).

Setting

A single-center, university-affiliated hospital.

Design

Retrospective comparative cohort study.

Methods

90 eyes of 45 patients who underwent bilateral cataract surgery after myopic LASIK were classified according to implanted IOL type: Full-DOFi Smooth (Tecnis Synergy), Partial-DOFi Enhanced (Eyhance), and Partial-DOFi Extended IOLs (PureSee). Distance-corrected visual acuity, monocular distance-corrected defocus curves, DOFi at 0.2 logMAR, refractive predictability with Barrett True-K TK and Haigis TK after IOL-specific optimization or mean prediction error zeroing, and patient-reported satisfaction were evaluated 3 months postoperatively.

Results

Corrected distance and intermediate visual acuities were comparable among groups (P = .967 and .780), whereas corrected near visual acuity differed (P < .001), favoring Full-DOFi Smooth, followed by Partial-DOFi Extended and Partial-DOFi Enhanced. DOFi was 3.22, 2.23, and 1.56 D, respectively. Prediction errors within ±0.50 D ranged from 76.7% to 83.3% with Barrett True-K TK and 70.0% to 73.3% with Haigis TK. Eyetemis analysis showed no trueness differences; Barrett True-K TK showed better precision and accuracy only in the Full-DOFi Smooth group. Near-vision satisfaction differed among groups, whereas pairwise glare/halo differences were not significant.

Conclusion

In selected post-myopic LASIK eyes, expected DOFi-based functional differences remained evident after correction of residual refractive error. Barrett True-K TK and Haigis TK showed generally comparable refractive performance. These findings indicate that DOFi-based functional classification remains clinically relevant in eyes with previous myopic LASIK.

records.title: Clinical Features, Phenotypic Spectrum, and Associated Factors in Histopathologically Confirmed Dead Bag Syndrome.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Clinical Features, Phenotypic Spectrum, and Associated Factors in Histopathologically Confirmed Dead Bag Syndrome.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To characterize the demographic, ocular, systemic, and histopathologic features of patients undergoing surgery for late intraocular lens (IOL) instability with clinically suspected dead bag syndrome (DBS).

Setting

Private ophthalmology practice and tertiary ophthalmic pathology laboratory.

Design

Single-center consecutive case series with prospective tissue collection and retrospective chart review.

Methods

Capsular bag remnants were explanted during secondary IOL surgery and submitted for histopathologic examination. Demographic, ocular, and systemic characteristics were obtained from the medical record. Lens epithelial cell (LEC) status was graded as 0 = absent; 1 = rare residual LECs; 2 = focal identifiable LEC segments. Specimens were assessed for capsular splitting/schisis, cortical material, and anterior capsular fibrous metaplasia. Exploratory clinical comparisons were performed between LEC grade 0 and LEC grade 1-2 subgroups.

Results

Thirty-one eyes from 26 patients underwent secondary IOL surgery for late IOL subluxation or dislocation with clinical suspicion of DBS, including 27 with histopathologic evaluation. Mean age at secondary surgery was 70.5 ± 10.5 years and 80.7% patients were male. Median time from cataract surgery to presentation was 13.0 years (IQR 9.0-16.5). Axial myopia was present in 6/31 eyes (19.4%). Atopy was documented in 9/31 (29.0%), prior radiation or chemotherapy exposure in 8/31 (25.8%), autoimmune disease in 10/31 (32.3%), and ACE inhibitor or ARB use in 14/31 (45.2%). Complete LEC absence (grade 0) was present in 8/27 (29.6%), while 19/27 (70.4%) demonstrated residual LECs and/or cortical material (grades 1-2). Spontaneous posterior capsular rupture was documented in 15/31 (48.4%) cases and in 15/27 (55.6%) histopathology-confirmed cases. Atopy was more frequent in LEC grade 0 than among LEC grade 1-2 eyes (37.5% vs 15.8%; P = 0.32), though this did not reach statistical significance.

Conclusions

DBS represents a histopathologically definable spectrum of capsular degeneration characterized by LEC depletion and capsular splitting with structural failure leading to late IOL instability. Nearly half of confirmed cases presented without clinically evident spontaneous posterior capsular rupture, suggesting that rupture is not required for DBS diagnosis.

records.title: Development of posterior vitreous detachment after lens surgery in myopic eyes - Results from the MYOPRED study.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Development of posterior vitreous detachment after lens surgery in myopic eyes - Results from the MYOPRED study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the preoperative posterior vitreous detachment (PVD) status and PVD progression in myopic eyes without preexisting complete PVD after lens surgery.

Setting

10 European study centers.

Design

Prospective observational multicenter study.

Methods

Eyes with an axial length of ≥25.0 mm scheduled for phacoemulsification were included. Preoperatively and at each visit, the PVD status was assessed by optical coherence tomography, at certain sites using additional ultrasonography. All patients had a follow-up visit 2 months postoperatively, those without preoperative complete PVD additionally at 6 and 12 months or until presence of complete PVD.

Results

In the analysis, 968 eyes (600 study eyes, 368 eligible fellow eyes) of 600 patients were considered. Mean age was 64.8±9.9 years (range 23-92), 290 (48.3%) were female, 310 (51.7%) male. At baseline, PVD was complete in 512 (52.9%) eyes, incomplete in 256 (26.4%), no PVD in 85 (8.8%) and 'not decisive' in 115 (11.9%). Of the eyes with no or incomplete PVD preoperatively, 9.9-12.6% developed a complete PVD by 2 months, 25.5% by 6 and 40.2% by 12 months (n=327). The hazard ratio for progression to complete PVD was 1.37 (CI 1.10-1.69, P=.003) for each decade of age and 1.25 (CI 1.11-1.54, P<.001) for each mm of axial length. PVD progression occurred in 48.0% of eyes within 12 months after surgery.

Conclusions

Four out of 10 myopic eyes with no or incomplete PVD preoperatively progressed to complete PVD within 1 year after phacoemulsification. Progression to complete PVD was associated with patient age and axial length.

records.title: Comparison of decentration, tilt, and dynamic stability between retropupillary iris claw and scleral-fixated intraocular lenses with flanged haptics.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Comparison of decentration, tilt, and dynamic stability between retropupillary iris claw and scleral-fixated intraocular lenses with flanged haptics.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare decentration, tilt, and dynamic stability ("wobble") between retropupillary-fixated iris claw intraocular lenses (IOLs) and double-needle flanged scleral-fixated technique.

Setting

Vienna Institute for Research in Ocular Surgery, Hanusch Hospital, Vienna, Austria.

Design

Monocentric comparative observational study.

Methods

Secondary IOL alignment was evaluated using swept source anterior segment optical coherence tomography to quantify decentration and tilt. Dynamic lens behavior was assessed using a Purkinje meter during 9-degree saccadic eye movements. Additional outcomes included visual acuity, refraction, and complications.

Results

72 eyes of 72 patients were included, comprising 31 eyes with retropupillary iris claw IOLs and 41 eyes with scleral-fixated IOLs. Mean decentration was similar between groups, with no statistically significant difference (598 ± 303 μm vs 535 ± 261 μm; P = .57). Mean tilt was lower in the iris claw group than in the scleral-fixated group, with a statistically significant difference between groups (6.52 ± 3.20 degrees vs 8.93 ± 5.02 degrees; P = .03). Across all gaze directions, iris claw lenses demonstrated greater dynamic instability, with larger postsaccadic oscillation amplitudes, longer stationary times, and lower damping ratios (all P < .001). Visual acuity, refraction, and complication rates were comparable between groups. The IOL-iris distance was smaller in the iris claw group.

Conclusions

Decentration was comparable, whereas iris claw lenses showed less tilt but greater dynamic instability than scleral-fixated lenses.

records.title: Effect of Dry Eye and Ocular Surface Treatment on Agreement and Repeatability of Corneal Astigmatism Measurements Among Three Devices.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Effect of Dry Eye and Ocular Surface Treatment on Agreement and Repeatability of Corneal Astigmatism Measurements Among Three Devices.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the effect of dry eye disease (DED) and ocular surface treatment on the agreement and repeatability of corneal astigmatism measurements obtained using IOLMaster 700, Pentacam, and iTrace in patients with age-related cataract.

Setting

Eye, Ear, Nose, and Throat Hospital of Fudan University, Shanghai, China.

Design

Prospective, single-center study.

Methods

A total of 313 eyes of patients with age-related cataract were included. Eyes with DED received 0.3% sodium hyaluronate eye drops for 2 weeks and were re-examined after treatment. Corneal astigmatism measurements were obtained using IOLMaster 700, Pentacam, and iTrace before pupil dilation. The main parameters included keratometric corneal astigmatism, total corneal astigmatism, and their vector components. Interdevice agreement was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis, and test-retest repeatability was evaluated using within-subject standard deviation, test-retest repeatability, and intraclass correlation coefficients.

Results

Compared with the control group, eyes at DED baseline showed wider limits of agreement and poorer TRT for both scalar astigmatism parameters and vector components. After ocular surface treatment, LoA width decreased by 50.5%-62.5% for KCA and 19.9%-29.0% for TCA across the three device comparisons. KCA repeatability improved significantly after treatment for IOLMaster 700 and iTrace, whereas significant improvement in TCA repeatability was observed only for IOLMaster 700. Device- and parameter-specific differences persisted after treatment.

Conclusions

DED was associated with reduced agreement and repeatability of corneal astigmatism measurements obtained using IOLMaster 700, Pentacam, and iTrace. Short-term ocular surface treatment was associated with improved measurement stability.

records.title: Biomechanical stiffening effect in ultra-high-fluence extracorporeal crosslinked corneal allogenic intrastromal ring segments.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Biomechanical stiffening effect in ultra-high-fluence extracorporeal crosslinked corneal allogenic intrastromal ring segments.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare the biomechanical stiffening effects of a new ultra-high-fluence corneal crosslinking (CXL) protocol with conventional high-fluence CXL for extracorporeal corneal allogenic intrastromal ring segment optimization (ECO-CAIRS).

Setting

ELZA Institute, Zurich, Switzerland.

Design

Experimental, randomized, controlled, ex vivo laboratory study using porcine corneas. No masking was applied.

Methods

84 porcine corneas were divided into 4 groups: Group A (control), Group B (10 J/cm 2 ), Group C (30 J/cm 2 ), and Group D (60 J/cm 2 ). After epithelial debridement, Groups B, C, and D were treated with 0.1% hypo-osmolar riboflavin. UV-A irradiation was delivered at fluences of 10 J/cm 2 (18 mW/cm 2 , 9:15 min) for Group B, 30 J/cm 2 (30 mW/cm 2 , 16:40 min) for Group C, and 60 J/cm 2 (30 mW/cm 2 , 33:18 min) for Group D. Corneal biomechanical properties were assessed by stress‑strain extensiometry.

Results

Mean elastic modulus (5% strain) values were as follows: Group A (1.39 ± 0.49 N/mm), Group B (1.83 ± 0.48 N/mm), Group C (2.25 ± 0.83 N/mm), and Group D (2.31 ± 0.88 N/mm). Ultra-high-fluence groups (C and D) showed significantly greater stiffening than Group B ( P = .041 and P = .015), with no significant difference between Groups C and D ( P = 1.00). Group B exhibited significantly greater stiffening than Group A ( P = .023).

Conclusions

Ultra-high-fluence CXL enhances biomechanical stiffening compared with conventional high-fluence CXL, supporting its use in ECO-CAIRS. In this extracorporeal context, endothelial safety and haze are irrelevant, while increased stiffness facilitates intrastromal ring insertion and reduces corneal swelling.

records.title: Uncorrected Visual Acuity and Visual Function Difficulties After Implantation of Simultaneous Vision Intraocular Lenses.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Uncorrected Visual Acuity and Visual Function Difficulties After Implantation of Simultaneous Vision Intraocular Lenses.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the association between binocular uncorrected visual acuity (UVA) at different distances and patient-reported difficulty with individual VF-14 activities after implantation of simultaneous vision intraocular lenses (SVIOLs).

Setting

("Masked by journal requirement").

Design

Retrospective observational.

Methods

Twelve-month data from 276 subjects implanted with either a Full-DOFi Smooth or a Partial-DOFi Extended IOL were included in the analysis. Visual acuities were obtained for far (UDVA, 4 m), intermediate (UIVA, 66 cm), and near (UNVA, 40 cm) distances, along with responses to a validated Spanish version of the VF-14 administered without spectacles. VF-14 responses were dichotomized (little/no vs other), and logistic regression analyses were performed to examine their associations with UDVA, UIVA, and UNVA. Statistical cut-off values were explored using the Youden index.

Results

UDVA was significantly associated with "traffic signs" and "night driving" (p < 0.05), whereas "watching TV" showed p = 0.06. UNVA was significantly associated with "knitting" (p < 0.05), whereas "large print" showed p = 0.06, and UIVA was associated with "newspapers" (p = 0.02). "Small print" and "knitting" were associated with both UIVA and UNVA, whereas "filling out forms" was associated only with UNVA (p < 0.05). Visual acuities were not associated with the remaining VF-14 items. Exploratory cut-off values maximizing the Youden index were generally 0.1 logMAR, except for "large print" (0.3 logMAR) and "traffic signs" (0.2 logMAR).

Conclusions

Only some VF-14 items were associated with binocular UVA. These findings may inform the development of PRO instruments for evaluating functional differences among SVIOLs.

records.title: Alignment Between Corneal Biomechanical Anisotropy and Toricity Using Optical Coherence Elastography.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Alignment Between Corneal Biomechanical Anisotropy and Toricity Using Optical Coherence Elastography.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the agreement in orientation and magnitude between corneal toricity and biomechanical anisotropy using optical coherence elastography (OCE).

Setting

College of Optometry, University of Houston, Houston, Texas, USA.

Design

Prospective cross-sectional study.

Methods

Healthy participants with spherical refractive error or corneal astigmatism > 0.50D were included. Corneal radial mechanical wave propagation speed, a proxy for corneal shear modulus, was measured using air-pulse wave-based OCE imaging (30° intervals over 360°). Biomechanical principal meridian () was defined as meridian with greatest wave speed, and its magnitude was calculated as difference between principal and orthogonal meridians. Likewise, astigmatic principal meridian () was defined as steep corneal meridian from videokeratography, and its magnitude was defined as dioptric difference between orthogonal steep and flat meridians. To compare these different domains (biomechanical anisotropy and astigmatism) within and across subjects, both vector magnitudes were cohort-normalized. Directional alignment between and was assessed using polar double-angle plots. Vectorial difference between these measures quantified similarities in both orientation and magnitude.

Results

30 eyes from 30 subjects were studied. Corneal astigmatism ranged from 0.15 to 3.66D (1.4±0.8D; mean±SD). Corneal wave speed in steep meridian was faster (12.97±1.6m/s) compared to flat meridian(9.03±1.8m/s). Biomechanical anisotropy strongly correlated with astigmatism (R2 = 0.88). Angular difference between and was 6.0°±7.1° among astigmatic eyes. Cohort-normalized magnitude difference between and was 0.06±0.07.

Conclusions

In vivo human corneal wave-based OCE measurements demonstrate that corneal biomechanical anisotropy exhibits an orthogonal pattern, highly correlated in orientation and magnitude with corneal topography.

records.title: Continuity of Care and Long-Term Outcome Surveillance After Posterior Chamber Phakic IOL Implantation.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Continuity of Care and Long-Term Outcome Surveillance After Posterior Chamber Phakic IOL Implantation.
content.abstract: Posterior chamber phakic intraocular lenses have a strong short-to-medium-term safety profile on the modern central-port platform, and a 2025 US Food and Drug Administration expansion of the indicated age range for a central-port phakic IOL to 21 to 60 years widens the eligible population. These lenses are to remain in the eye for decades, yet the field has defined what to monitor without building the infrastructure to deliver that monitoring reliably as patients age, change providers, and relocate. Existing guidance specifies endothelial and vault thresholds but does not address who monitors after the implanting surgeon, how baseline and longitudinal data transfer, or how late events are learned across practices. We propose three measures: upgrading the implant identification card into a longitudinal, portable surveillance record; a risk-stratified, age-informed surveillance framework developed through multisociety consensus; and a prospective implant registry with a defined minimum dataset. The device's clinical maturation now requires a parallel evolution in its care model.

records.title: Treatment-induced changes in higher-order aberrations after ray-tracing-guided vs. wavefront-optimized laser in situ keratomileusis.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Treatment-induced changes in higher-order aberrations after ray-tracing-guided vs. wavefront-optimized laser in situ keratomileusis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Intraindividual comparison of treatment-induced changes of ocular higher-order aberrations (HOAs) after ray-tracing-guided laser in situ keratomileusis (LASIK) and wavefront-optimized LASIK.

Setting

University hospital.

Design

Prospective, randomized, eye-to-eye comparative study.

Methods

Patients with myopia and myopic astigmatism underwent ray-tracing-guided wavelight plus (Alcon) LASIK in one eye and wavefront-optimized LASIK in the fellow eye. The study assessed treatment-induced changes (3 months postoperative - preoperative) in root-mean-square (RMS) of total HOAs, primary spherical aberration, RMS coma and RMS trefoil after wavelight plus and wavefront-optimized LASIK.

Results

Thirty patients (sixty eyes) were included in the study. The mean change (± standard deviation) in RMS of total HOAs at 6-mm zone of analysis was 0.00±0.15µm after wavelight plus (p=0.758) and 0.11±0.12µm after wavefront-optimized LASIK (p<0.001). A negative spherical aberration change of -0.07±0.13µm (p=0.012) occurred after wavelight plus and a positive change of 0.06±0.09µm (p<0.001) after wavefront-optimized treatment. Changes in coma and trefoil were 0.02±0.15µm (p=0.474) and -0.02±0.10µm (p=0.225) after wavelight plus, while after wavefront-optimized LASIK they were respectively, 0.10±0.13µm (p<0.001) and 0.02±0.06µm (p=0.058). In contralateral-eye comparison, wavelight plus resulted in lower total HOAs in all patients with elevated preoperative HOAs (RMS of total HOAs >0.30µm, n=13 patients) and in 70.6% of patients (n=12) with low preoperative HOAs (≤0.30µm, n=17 patients).

Conclusions

Wavefront-optimized LASIK increased total HOAs, spherical aberration and coma, while no increase in HOAs was detected after wavelight plus. Spherical aberration decreased (negative change) after wavelight plus. The benefit of ray-tracing-guided LASIK tended to be larger in patients with higher preoperative HOAs.

records.title: Long-Term Visual, Refractive, and Patient-Reported Satisfaction of the Tel-Aviv Protocol (ePRK-CXL) for Progressive Keratoconus.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Long-Term Visual, Refractive, and Patient-Reported Satisfaction of the Tel-Aviv Protocol (ePRK-CXL) for Progressive Keratoconus.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the long-term visual, refractive, and patient-reported satisfaction of epithelial photorefractive keratectomy (ePRK) combined with corneal cross-linking (CXL) - the Tel-Aviv Protocol - in patients with progressive keratoconus.

Setting

Care-Vision Laser Center, Tel Aviv, Israel.

Design

Retrospective, single-center case series.

Methods

Consecutive patients with progressive keratoconus who underwent ePRK-CXL were included. Preoperative and last-available postoperative pachymetry, keratometry (Kmean, Kmin, Kmax), spherical equivalent (SEQ), manifest refraction, uncorrected distance visual acuity (UDVA), and corrected distance visual acuity (CDVA) were recorded; safety and efficacy indices were calculated. Patient-reported outcomes regarding spectacle/contact lens dependence, satisfaction, and visual symptoms were assessed with a structured questionnaire.

Results

Fifty eyes of 38 patients (mean age 25.9±6.8 years) were followed for a mean of 2,910±605 days (∼8 years; range 5-12). UDVA improved from 1.04±0.70 to 0.36±0.37 logMAR and CDVA from 0.23±0.16 to 0.11±0.10 logMAR (both P < 0.001); safety and efficacy indices were 1.42±0.55 and 0.93±0.51. K-max decreased from 47.51±2.96 to 45.95±2.99 D and SEQ from -2.42±2.29 to -0.82±1.57 D (both P < 0.001). Pachymetry decreased from 448.65±38.95 to 418.93±55.77 μm. Overall satisfaction was high (81.6% satisfied/very satisfied), 76.3% reported subjective visual improvement, 52.6% achieved spectacle independence, and 92.1% required no contact lenses. No progression was observed in the examined eyes.

Conclusions

At a mean follow-up of ∼8 years, the Tel-Aviv Protocol provided durable visual and refractive improvement, stabilized keratometry without progression, and yielded high patient satisfaction with low symptom burden. These results support ePRK-CXL as a tissue-sparing option for progressive keratoconus.

records.title: Resident to Urgent Eye Clinic Transformation and Association With Health Equity and Resident Education.

content.title: Resident to Urgent Eye Clinic Transformation and Association With Health Equity and Resident Education.
content.abstract:
Importance

US ophthalmology residency programs are divided between traditional resident clinic-based models with a separate faculty practice, and universal practice-based models. Little data exist comparing these educational models.

Objective

To evaluate the association of changing a traditional resident clinic training model to a universal practice plus urgent eye clinic-based residency training model with sociodemographic disparities and resident education.

Design, setting, and participants

This was a cross-sectional study conducted at a US academic medical center. All patients presenting to the University of Rochester Flaum Eye Institute between the period July 1, 2017, to June 30, 2019, and the period July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2024, were divided into 4 cohorts for retrospective analysis as follows: resident clinic 2017-2019, faculty practice 2017-2019, urgent eye clinic 2022-2024, and universal practice 2022-2024.

Exposures

The resident clinic was transitioned to urgent eye clinic in July 2022. All former patients from resident clinic were reassigned to the new universal practice.

Main outcomes and measures

Patient cohorts were compared regarding insurance payor(s) and self-identified race. Level of disease acuity in resident clinic and urgent eye clinic were compared. Graduating resident procedural volumes were compared.

Results

Participants were divided into the following 4 cohorts: resident clinic 2017-2019 (6819 patients), faculty practice 2017-2019 (61 847 patients), urgent eye clinic 2022-2024 (5124 patients), and universal practice 2022-2024 (79 001 patients), for a total of 118 459 patients (mean [SD] age, 47 [25] years; 65 186 female [55%]). Pretransition, compared with faculty practice patients, greater proportions of resident clinic patients used Medicaid insurance (62.1% vs 19.4%; difference, 32.0%; 95% CI, 30.9%-33.1%; P < .001) and identified as Asian, Black or African American, multiracial, native (ie, American Indian or Alaska Native), or other (51.9% vs 23.6%; difference, 28.3%; 95% CI, 27.1%-29.5%; P < .001). Posttransition, compared with universal practice patients, similar proportions of urgent eye clinic patients used Medicaid insurance (26.8% vs 27.8%; difference, 0.4%; 95% CI, -0.7% to 1.6%; P = .42) and identified as Asian, Black or African American, multiracial, native, or other (29.6% vs 26.8%; difference, 2.8%; 95% CI, 1.5%-4.1%; P < .001). A greater proportion of urgent eye clinic patients presented with high-acuity disease (37.6%) compared with resident clinic patients (20.9%; difference, 16.7%; 95% CI, 15.0%-18.4%; P < .001). Median graduating resident primary cataract surgery volume increased from 148 to 228 cases (difference, 80; 95% CI, 49 to 122; P < .001).

Conclusions and relevance

Results of this cross-sectionals study show that transforming resident clinic into urgent eye clinic was associated with reduced sociodemographic disparities, enhanced resident exposure to high-acuity disease, and increased resident procedural experience. These results suggest that changes in resident clinic structure may improve both health equity and resident education.

records.title: Standardising ocular surface photography for artificial intelligence: current limitations and a proposed roadmap.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Standardising ocular surface photography for artificial intelligence: current limitations and a proposed roadmap.
content.abstract: Slit-lamp colour photography remains a cornerstone of anterior segment documentation and longitudinal monitoring. However, conventional slit-lamp photography has seen relatively limited technological advancement compared with the rapid development of quantitative anterior-segment modalities such as AS-OCT, Scheimpflug tomography and confocal microscopy. Despite the wide diffusion of digital cameras, smartphones, and high-end slit-lamp systems, ocular surface photography (OSP) remains hampered by the absence of standardised acquisition and processing protocols. The convex, aspheric geometry of the ocular surface, off-axis illumination, peripheral defocus, automatic colour correction, and pupil-driven exposure variation in retroillumination limit reproducibility, inter-device comparability, and clinical utility. In this review we critically appraise current OSP applications across major ocular surface conditions (dry eye disease, conjunctival hyperaemia, infectious keratitis, ocular surface burns, and ocular surface neoplasia), mapping the hardware, software, and reproducibility limitations that constrain clinical practice. We then examine how these limitations propagate into artificial intelligence (AI) development, where the absence of large, well-annotated, demographically diverse OSP datasets, together with the lack of reproducible quantitative phenotypes and reliable labels, is now the principal bottleneck to clinically deployable models; we discuss patient-level data partitioning and external validation, and outline how deep learning, federated learning and foundation models can both utilise and improve OSP. Finally, we propose a minimum acquisition and dataset specification, tiered by clinical setting from research to community screening, and a staged roadmap that combines hardware standardisation (focus-stacked, illumination-controlled, colour-calibrated acquisition), interoperable metadata-rich storage (DICOM where infrastructure permits), quantitative phenotype definition, and diverse international dataset collaborations, so that the ocular surface can benefit from quantitative imaging and AI as other areas of ophthalmology have begun to.

records.title: Changing Patterns of Dry Eye Disease Management in Korea: A Nationwide 10-Year Analysis.

content.title: Changing Patterns of Dry Eye Disease Management in Korea: A Nationwide 10-Year Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate long-term trends in treated dry eye disease (DED) prevalence and medication prescribing patterns in Korea using a nationwide mandatory insurance claims database.

Design

Retrospective nationwide clinical cohort study.

Participants

Patients identified from the Korean NHIS mandatory claims database (2014-2023).

Methods

DED was defined by at least one relevant ICD-10 diagnosis code together with at least one prescription for a DED-related topical medication within the same calendar year. Annual overall, sex-specific, and age-specific prevalence was calculated using the corresponding mid-year resident population. Medication classes and single-use versus multi-use formulations were evaluated. Medication use in Sjögren syndrome-associated versus non-Sjögren DED was compared using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age and sex.

Main outcome measures

Annual treated DED prevalence, medication prescribing proportions, formulation-specific prescribing trends, and differences between Sjögren syndrome-associated and non-Sjögren syndrome DED.

Results

Approximately 61.8 million patient-years were analyzed, representing 9.87 million unique patients. Annual treated DED prevalence ranged from 4.84% to 5.61% and was consistently higher in women and older individuals. Hyaluronic acid (HA) remained the most prescribed medication, although its proportional share declined from 85.03% in 2014 to 76.89% in 2023 (P < .001). Diquafosol prescriptions increased from 4.61% to 10.77%, and cyclosporine prescriptions increased from 2.39% to 5.77% (both P < .001). Single-use HA prescriptions increased from 39.73% to 73.76% (P < .001), and single-use diquafosol accounted for 61.8% of diquafosol prescriptions by 2023. Cyclosporine was prescribed to 26.00% of patients with Sjögren syndrome-associated DED and 7.51% of those with non-Sjögren DED; the adjusted OR was 4.06 (95% CI, 3.99-4.12).

Conclusions

Over the past decade, DED management in Korea shifted toward the anti-inflammatory cyclosporine, the mucin and water secretagogue diquafosol, and preservative-free single-use formulations. Patients with Sjögren syndrome-associated DED demonstrated distinct prescribing patterns, including substantially greater cyclosporine use after adjustment for age and sex.

records.title: Validation of the University of California, Irvine Corneal Cystine Crystal Score (UCI CCCS): Correlations with Clinical, Imaging, and Symptom Outcomes in Cystinosis.

content.title: Validation of the University of California, Irvine Corneal Cystine Crystal Score (UCI CCCS): Correlations with Clinical, Imaging, and Symptom Outcomes in Cystinosis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To prospectively validate the University of California, Irvine Corneal Cystine Crystal Score (UCI CCCS), a standardized slit-lamp grading tool, by evaluating associations with objective corneal densitometry, patient-reported symptoms, and visual acuity in a real-world cystinosis cohort.

Design

Prospective observational cross-sectional study.

Participants

Seventy patients (140 eyes) with confirmed cystinosis were examined at the 2024-2025 Cystinosis Research Foundation Day of Hope Clinics.

Methods

All eyes underwent live slit-lamp UCI CCCS grading (0-5). Pentacam Scheimpflug densitometry was obtained in 68 eyes. Two ophthalmologists independently graded patients during the 2025 clinic to assess inter-rater reliability. Patient-reported symptoms, best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), and topical cysteamine treatment data were collected. Linear mixed-effects models accounting for within-patient correlation were used for densitometry and BCVA analyses. Symptom associations were evaluated at the patient level using Kendall's tau-b.

Main outcome measures

Inter-rater reliability of UCI CCCS; associations with corneal densitometry, patient-reported symptoms, and BCVA.

Results

Inter-rater reliability was excellent (ICC = 0.995; 95% CI, 0.992-0.996). Linear mixed-effects modeling demonstrated significant associations between UCI CCCS grade and central (p = 0.0016) and anterior corneal densitometry (p = 0.0011) after accounting for within-patient correlation between fellow eyes. Higher UCI CCCS grades were significantly associated with greater photophobia (τ = 0.397, p < 0.0001), foreign-body sensation (τ = 0.295, p = 0.0047), and ocular dryness (τ = 0.405, p = 0.0001). No statistically significant association was observed between UCI CCCS grade and BCVA after accounting for within-patient correlation (p = 0.4389). No significant differences in UCI CCCS or corneal densitometry were observed across topical cysteamine treatment groups.

Conclusion

The UCI CCCS is a highly reproducible, clinically practical grading tool associated with objective corneal densitometry and patient-reported symptom burden, while BCVA was not significantly associated with UCI CCCS grade. Longitudinal studies are needed to evaluate treatment responsiveness and prognostic value.

records.title: STRUCTURE-FUNCTION ASSOCIATION BETWEEN CONTRAST SENSITIVITY FUNCTION AND OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY FEATURES IN PATIENTS WITH IDIOPATHIC EPIRETINAL MEMBRANE.

content.title: STRUCTURE-FUNCTION ASSOCIATION BETWEEN CONTRAST SENSITIVITY FUNCTION AND OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY FEATURES IN PATIENTS WITH IDIOPATHIC EPIRETINAL MEMBRANE.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Investigate the structure-function relationships between epiretinal membrane (ERM) stage, tractional abnormalities, and the gap area between the ERM and the retinal surface, in relation to visual acuity and quantitative contrast sensitivity function in patients with idiopathic epiretinal membrane.

Methods

This was a retrospective, cross-sectional study involving 111 participants diagnosed with idiopathic ERM. All patients underwent a comprehensive ophthalmologic examination, spectral-domain optical coherence tomography imaging using the SPECTRALIS Heidelberg system, and contrast sensitivity (CS) testing using the quantitative contrast sensitivity function method.

Results

Progressive stages of ERM were associated with declines in both CS and visual acuity (β* = -0.45 to -0.19, P < 0.02), with CS showing a more pronounced reduction than visual acuity, especially between controls and Stage 1. Ectopic inner foveal layer thickness exhibited a similar pattern of decline in both visual acuity (β* = 0.42, P < 0.001) and CS (β* = -0.46 to -0.18, all P < 0.02). By contrast, SUKIMA showed no significant association with any of the visual measurements assessed. Among the tractional abnormalities, the cotton ball sign correlated with diminished vision, particularly reflected by a notable drop in CS at the highest spatial frequencies tested with reduced CS at 12 cycles per degree (β* = -0.44, P = 0.02) and 18 cycles per degree (β* = -0.46, P = 0.02).

Conclusion

Quantitative contrast sensitivity function testing is particularly important for assessing visual function in ERM development, especially in the early stages.

records.title: AI-ASSISTED OCT BIOMARKER QUANTIFICATION REVEALS DISTINCT RETINAL FLUID TRAJECTORIES IN CENTRAL RETINAL VEIN OCCLUSION.

content.title: AI-ASSISTED OCT BIOMARKER QUANTIFICATION REVEALS DISTINCT RETINAL FLUID TRAJECTORIES IN CENTRAL RETINAL VEIN OCCLUSION.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To characterize longitudinal patterns of intraretinal (IRF) and subretinal fluid (SRF) dynamics using artificial intelligence-assisted optical coherence tomography (OCT) biomarker quantification and to evaluate their association with long-term visual outcomes in eyes with central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO).

Methods

Patients with previously treatment-naïve CRVO and a documented 24-month follow-up were retrospectively included. All eyes received intravitreal aflibercept administered according to a treat-and-extend protocol. Spectral-domain OCT scans were analyzed at baseline and after 3 and 24 months. IRF and SRF volumes were quantified using RetinAI Discovery OCT Biomarker Detector (Ikerian AG). Linear regression models were used to assess the association between fluid volumes and 24-month corrected distance visual acuity (CDVA). Patients were clustered according to their IRF trajectories over time to identify distinct fluid-response phenotypes.

Results

Out of 173 patients, 64 eyes (64 patients) were included. Baseline IRF and SRF volumes showed no significant association with 24-month CDVA. Cluster analysis of longitudinal IRF trajectories identified four distinct fluid-response patterns. Eyes with low or rapidly resolving IRF achieved the best long-term visual outcomes (median CDVA 73 letters), whereas those with persistent or recurrent IRF showed poorer outcomes (median 53 letters; P = 0.008). Early IRF resolution tended to predict superior visual recovery at 24 months.

Conclusion

Artificial intelligence-based volumetric OCT analysis suggests that distinct retinal fluid trajectories in CRVO may have prognostic implications for long-term visual acuity, although these findings are preliminary and require validation. Dynamic IRF resolution patterns may be more informative than static fluid volumes for predicting functional outcomes after anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapy.

records.title: Association of Retinal Microvascular Density with Hemodynamic and Clinical Severity Markers in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.

content.title: Association of Retinal Microvascular Density with Hemodynamic and Clinical Severity Markers in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate whether quantitative retinal microvascular and structural parameters, measured by optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA), are associated with disease severity and right ventriculo-arterial coupling in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH).

Methods

This cross-sectional study included 45 patients with confirmed PAH, stratified by New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class (I-III). Patients with coexisting ocular pathologies were strictly excluded. Vessel density (VD) in the superficial (SCP) and deep capillary plexuses (DCP), foveal avascular zone characteristics, and ganglion cell complex (GCC) thickness were analyzed. These parameters were correlated with functional capacity (6-minute walk test [6-mWT]), NT-proBNP levels, and the echocardiographic TAPSE/sPAP ratio.

Results

Retinal VD in both SCP and DCP progressively decreased with worsening NYHA functional class (p < 0.05). Retinal VD showed a significant negative correlation with NT-proBNP levels (r = -0.355, p = 0.017) and a positive correlation with 6-mWT distance (r = 0.499, p < 0.001). Crucially, retinal microvascular density demonstrated a robust positive correlation with the TAPSE/sPAP ratio (r = 0.420, p = 0.004), a surrogate for right ventriculo-arterial coupling. GCC thickness exhibited variations across NYHA classes but lacked a consistent linear progression.

Conclusion

Retinal microvascular attenuation in PAH is strongly associated not only with functional and biochemical severity but also with central hemodynamic impairment represented by the TAPSE/sPAP ratio. These findings suggest that OCTA-derived vessel density may serve as a promising, non-invasive biomarker for monitoring systemic microvascular compromise and right heart function in PAH.
