records.title: RISK OF INTRAOCULAR INFLAMMATION AFTER INJECTION OF ANTIVASCULAR ENDOTHELIAL GROWTH FACTOR AGENTS: A Meta-analysis.

content.title: RISK OF INTRAOCULAR INFLAMMATION AFTER INJECTION OF ANTIVASCULAR ENDOTHELIAL GROWTH FACTOR AGENTS: A Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

This meta-analysis investigates the incidence of intraocular inflammation (IOI) after intravitreal antivascular endothelial growth factor injections in neovascular age-related macular degeneration.

Methods

A systematic search was performed on Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane Central from January 2005 to April 2021. Randomized controlled trials comparing IOI after intravitreal bevacizumab, ranibizumab, brolucizumab, or aflibercept in neovascular age-related macular degeneration were included. Primary outcomes were sight-threatening IOI, final best-corrected visual acuity, and change in best-corrected visual acuity from baseline. Secondary outcomes included the incidence of other IOI events. Meta-analysis was performed using a random-effects model.

Results

Overall, 11,460 unique studies were screened, of which 14 randomized controlled trials and 6,759 eyes at baseline were included. There was no difference between agents for the risk of endophthalmitis and retinal vascular occlusion. Compared with aflibercept, brolucizumab had a higher incidence of generalized IOI (risk ratio = 6.24, 95% confidence interval = [1.40-27.90]) and vitreous haze/floaters (risk ratio = 1.64, 95% confidence interval = [1.00-2.67]). There were no significant differences between comparators for other secondary end points.

Conclusion

There was no difference in the risk of severe sight-threatening IOI outcomes between intravitreal antivascular endothelial growth factor agents. There was a significantly higher risk of generalized IOI after brolucizumab relative to aflibercept. Our results alongside other recent safety findings suggest the need for further investigation in the risk-benefit profile of brolucizumab for the treatment of neovascular age-related macular degeneration.

records.title: Challenges to the Access and Utilization of Corneal Cross-Linking in Patients With Keratoconus in the United States.

content.title: Challenges to the Access and Utilization of Corneal Cross-Linking in Patients With Keratoconus in the United States.
content.abstract:
Objective or purpose

To investigate current disparities in access to corneal cross-linking (CXL) for patients with keratoconus in the United States and to anticipate further disparities in the wake of Epioxa approval and planned Photrexa phasing out.

Design

Perspective essay.

Methods, intervention, or testing

This essay reflects on experiences from all authors in their care for patients with keratoconus, a historical summary of CXL in the United States, and a literature review.

Results

CXL has been proven to slow the progression of keratoconus and reduce the need for corneal transplants. Currently, there is only 1 Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved epithelium-off CXL protocol in the United States (KXL system using Photrexa or Photrexa Viscous), and its access has been limited by high costs, insurance coverage, and proprietary protocols. The result is that underserved patients have had reduced access to treatment. In 2025, the FDA approved Epioxa, an epithelium-on CXL therapy, under an orphan drug designation. In addition to concerns surrounding affordability, it is uncertain whether Epioxa has comparable short- and long-term effectiveness to Photrexa in terms of visual acuity and maximum keratometry. With Epioxa's recently reported wholesale acquisition cost of $78,500, the authors feel the need to advocate for patients who will be unable to receive these potentially vision-saving therapies. Further concerning is that Photrexa will be phased out in 2026, meaning there will no longer be an FDA-approved epithelium-off CXL therapy available in the United States.

Conclusions

With the approval of Epioxa and the planned phasing out of Photrexa, we underscore the risk of exacerbating disparities in access to CXL and propose the formation of an interdisciplinary task force aimed at developing an access framework for CXL therapy for all patients. We believe that the first step is to pause the phasing out of Photrexa until (1) there is a formalized plan in place to combat the issues of CXL access as detailed here and (2) the long-term efficacy of Epioxa can be sufficiently demonstrated.

records.title: Retinal Pigment Epithelium and Microglia Transplantation in Age-related Macular Degeneration.

content.title: Retinal Pigment Epithelium and Microglia Transplantation in Age-related Macular Degeneration.
content.abstract: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) remains a leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide, characterized by the progressive breakdown of the outer blood-retinal barrier, accumulation of protein and lipid deposits in the subretinal space, and the consequential degeneration of macular photoreceptors. Geographic atrophy (GA) is one of the blinding end points of AMD. While current pharmaceutical interventions can slow lesion expansion or counter choroidal neovascularization, they fail to address the most significant clinical unmet need: regeneration of damaged retinal tissue to restore vision. Regenerative medicine via stem cell transplantation offers a definitive curative approach by replacing the structural and immune framework of the outer retina. This review synthesizes current advancements in human embryonic and pluripotent stem cells platforms engineered for outer retinal reconstruction. We evaluate the differentiation, culturing, and quality validation required to generate clinical-grade, polarized RPE monolayers and homeostatic microglia-like cells. Structurally, single-cell suspensions are contrasted against bioengineered patches, scaffold-free cell sheets, and advanced cell strips, analyzing how graft configuration dictates post-transplantation integration and visual recovery while balancing procedural adverse events like cell reflux and epiretinal membrane formation. Furthermore, this review addresses the microenvironmental challenges of transplanting allogeneic constructs into an inflamed, senescent host niche. We examine CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing paradigms, including cytosine base and prime editing, designed to rectify cell-intrinsic genetic vulnerabilities such as the complement factor H (CFH) risk variant. We highlight translational applications, such as knocking out the Class II transactivator to eliminate major histocompatibility complex class II (MHC-II) expression, which successfully circumvents host T-cell immune surveillance and prevents graft rejection in non-human primates. Additionally, we analyze how engineering an inhibitor-resistant colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor (CSF1R) point mutation enables exogenously administered microglia to robustly outcompete and replace maladaptive, pro-inflammatory host microglia under selective small-molecule pressure. Finally, we discuss future directions, emphasizing multi-lineage bilayered co-transplantation models that combine genome-edited RPE patches with homeostatic microglia or retinal organoids to achieve durable synaptic repair, alongside automated artificial intelligence manufacturing pipelines. Together, these combined structural, molecular, and immune-modulating strategies represent the next clinical frontier in restoring clear central vision and achieving permanent neurovascular rescue in advanced macular degeneration.

records.title: Efficacy, Safety, and Durability of Gene Therapy for Inherited Retinal Diseases in the Pediatric Population: A Scoping Review.

content.title: Efficacy, Safety, and Durability of Gene Therapy for Inherited Retinal Diseases in the Pediatric Population: A Scoping Review.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To map the published interventional gene-based therapies relevant to children with inherited retinal diseases (IRDs), with a focus on efficacy, safety, and durability, including pediatric-vs-adult patterns where available.

Methods

This scoping review followed a prospectively registered protocol specifying the search strategy, eligibility criteria, screening process, data-charting framework, and synthesis plan. PubMed and Embase were searched from January 1, 2008, to April 13, 2026. Retrieved records were independently screened by 2 reviewers to identify prospective interventional studies of gene-targeted therapies for molecularly confirmed IRDs enrolling participants younger than 18 years; unresolved disagreements were adjudicated by a third reviewer. Overlapping reports were grouped into trial clusters with a primary anchor record. Records with at least 3 pediatric participants and separately extractable pediatric data were classified as Tier 1 and included in the main synthesis; other eligible records were retained as Tier 2 contextual evidence. Where sufficient individual-level or subgroup-level data were available, review authors extracted descriptive pediatric-vs-adult patterns.

Results

Twenty-four records, grouped into 17 trial clusters across 8 genotypes, were included; 14 met Tier 1 criteria. RPE65-associated disease provided the largest pediatric evidence base and the most consistent efficacy and durability signals, although responses varied between trial clusters. AIPL1 gene supplementation showed substantial treated-eye functional gains with relative structural preservation at up to 4 years in 4 very young children, and high-dose GUCY2D gene supplementation improved retinal sensitivity in 3 children within a mixed-age cohort. CEP290-targeted splice modulation and gene editing showed early functional signals, but interpretation was limited by dose-related cataract with sepofarsen and few pediatric participants with EDIT-101. Evidence for RPGR, CNGB3, RS1, and MERTK did not support robust pediatric-specific efficacy conclusions. Serious ocular events were predominantly procedure-related, with no reproducible pediatric-specific toxicity signal. Formal age-stratified analyses were uncommon, and several pediatric-vs-adult patterns required review-author extraction.

Conclusions

Pediatric benefit from IRD gene therapy depends on genotype, residual retinal structure, therapeutic platform, dose, surgical strategy, and outcome measure. The major evidence gaps are long-term pediatric durability and inconsistent age-stratified reporting. Future pediatric-inclusive trials should prespecify subgroup analyses, embed prospective long-term follow-up, use developmentally appropriate endpoints, and report individual-level data sufficient to support pediatric inference.

records.title: Inventory of Ocular Pulse Amplitude Values in Healthy Subjects and Patients With Ophthalmologic Illnesses: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

content.title: Inventory of Ocular Pulse Amplitude Values in Healthy Subjects and Patients With Ophthalmologic Illnesses: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Many studies have examined the ocular pulse amplitude (OPA) to better understand its physiology and clinical relevance, but the papers are scattered, not consistently indexed, and sometimes difficult to locate. We aimed to identify and summarize the relevant published evidence on OPA and, in a meta-analysis, outline specific differences of this parameter between healthy individual, primary open-angle glaucoma, normal-tension glaucoma, ocular hypertension, and cataract patients.

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis.

Methods

A thorough literature search and data extraction were conducted by 2 reviewers independently. Reports on OPA measured by the dynamic contour tonometry in conjunction with different ocular and systemic diseases or potential influencing factors were included.

Results

Of the 527 initially found reports, 97 met the inclusion criteria assessing 31 clinical conditions. A meta-analysis based on 6850 eyes and 106 study arms (68.8%) revealed differences in mean OPA values in millimeters of mercury between various entities. Among healthy eyes, the OPA was 2.58 mm Hg (95% CI: 2.45-2.71), whereas OPA values were higher in glaucoma (unspecified glaucoma 2.73 mm Hg, 95% CI: 2.38-3.08; normal-tension glaucoma 2.66 mm Hg, 95% CI: 2.36-2.97; and primary open-angle glaucoma 2.92 mm Hg, 95% CI: 2.75-3.08). Although ocular hypertension showed the highest OPA values (3.53 mm Hg, 95% CI: 3.05-4.01), the lowest values were found in cataract eyes (2.26 mm Hg, 95% CI: 1.57-2.94).

Conclusion

We found different OPA values characteristic of different clinical entities, with above-normal values in glaucoma and ocular hypertension and lower values in cataract patients. Our work is intended for clinicians and researchers who want to get a quick overview of the available evidence or who need statistical data on OPA distributions in individual diseases.

records.title: Outcomes and Complications of Pars Plana Vitrectomy for Tractional Retinal Detachment in People With Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

content.title: Outcomes and Complications of Pars Plana Vitrectomy for Tractional Retinal Detachment in People With Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Importance

Tractional retinal detachment (TRD) occurs in approximately 5% of people with proliferative diabetic retinopathy and poses a threat to vision. Pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) is the treatment of choice for TRD.

Objective

To determine anatomic and functional outcomes of PPV for the treatment of TRD in people with diabetes (dTRD).

Data sources

MEDLINE and Embase were searched systematically from January 1, 2000, to February 20, 2022. In addition, a reference list of eligible studies were screened.

Study selection

Eligible studies were those published in English, those reporting outcomes of PPV for dTRD, and those that included more than 25 eyes and with a minimum follow-up of 3 months.

Data extraction and synthesis

Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses (PRISMA) guidelines for data extraction/synthesis were followed, and the National Institute for Health quality assessment tool was used to assess risk of bias. Study eligibility was determined independently by 2 reviewers; data extraction was conducted by 1 reviewer and entries checked for accuracy by another. Data were pooled using a random-effects model.

Main outcomes and measures

Main outcomes included rate of failure of retinal reattachment following 1 surgery and final visual acuity (VA). The association of baseline patient characteristics and surgical maneuvers with postoperative surgical outcomes was investigated.

Results

Of the 406 studies identified, 38 (3839 eyes) were eligible and included for analysis. Patients had a median (IQR) age of 52.2 (49.6-55.7) years. In the studies reporting patient sex (31 of 38 studies), 1441 were female individuals (50.1%). The overall failure rate of retinal reattachment after 1 surgery was 5.9% (95% CI, 1.4%-8.3%), and the mean final VA was 0.94 (95% CI, 0.82-1.05) logMAR (approximate Snellen equivalent, 6/53; 95% CI, 6/39-6/71). People with higher preoperative VA achieved higher postoperative vision (0.66 logMAR worse final vision; 95% CI, 0.39-0.84 per 1.0 logMAR worse at baseline; P <.001). On multivariable analysis, no other patient characteristics or surgical variables had a statistically significant association with outcomes.

Conclusions and relevance

Results of this systematic review and meta-analysis suggest that PPV was an effective strategy to achieve retinal reattachment in people with dTRD. Given that higher preoperative VA was the only factor associated with higher postoperative vision, early intervention should be considered and discussed in detail with patients. Overall, final postoperative VA remains low, and patients should be counseled on the guarded prognosis of dTRD.

records.title: Beyond convolutions and supervised learning with transformers and representation learning for retinal image analysis.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Beyond convolutions and supervised learning with transformers and representation learning for retinal image analysis.
content.abstract: Retinal image analysis has enjoyed groundbreaking advances in the last ten years due to seismic improvements in image analysis techniques from the field of computer vision. Previous reviews in deep learning and artificial intelligence (AI) (Schmidt-Erfurth et al., 2018; Ting et al., 2019) have either focused on supervised learning, where labels are curated or manually created, or concentrated on the application of AI in specific image modalities and retina diseases (Hormel et al., 2021; Li et al., 2024a (Hormel et al., 2021; Li et al., 2024a)). In this review, we sought to summarize the advances in the field with the shift towards label-free approaches using representational learning and the emergence of vision transformers as alternatives to convolutional neural networks for image analysis. These advances include semi-supervised learning, self-supervised learning and directly led to the advent of foundation models, vision-language models, and multi-modal models.

records.title: EFFICIENCY OF LASER PHOTOCOAGULATION ON THE PREVENTION OF RETINAL DETACHMENT IN ACUTE RETINAL NECROSIS: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: EFFICIENCY OF LASER PHOTOCOAGULATION ON THE PREVENTION OF RETINAL DETACHMENT IN ACUTE RETINAL NECROSIS: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Retinal detachment is a severe complication of acute retinal necrosis, threatening vision. The published articles on the effectiveness of laser in preventing retinal detachment in acute retinal necrosis are controversial. Therefore, we aim to evaluate whether prophylactic laser is effective for retinal detachment after acute retinal necrosis.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane databases were searched, and the retrieved records were screened. Each included study has well-defined laser-treated group and control group without laser treatment or with enough data for manual grouping. The quality of the included studies was assessed using ROBINS-I ("Risk Of Bias In Nonrandomized Studies-of Interventions"). Meta-analysis was conducted to calculate the pooled odds ratios and their 95% confidence interval. Sensitivity analysis was used to test the solidarity, and subgroup analysis was performed to determine the source of heterogeneity.

Results

Fourteen studies with a total of 532 eyes were eventually included. The quality of the included studies was moderate. The combined results showed that the pooled odds ratio was 0.61 (95% confidence interval [0.41∼0.90], P < 0.05, I 2 = 27%). Sensitivity analysis showed that the odds ratios were similar when excluding any study. Subgroup analysis showed moderate heterogeneity among three subgroups (I 2 = 48.0%, P = 0.15 for heterogeneity), and the odds ratio in antiviral therapy and steroid combined with prophylactic laser was 0.43 (95% confidence interval [0.25∼0.74], P < 0.05, I 2 = 0%).

Conclusion

In patients with acute retinal necrosis, laser photocoagulation is an effective treatment to prevent retinal detachment, especially in the subgroup combined with antiviral therapy and steroid.

records.title: Future direction of corneal transplantation with new and innovative options for keratoconus and ectasia: descriptive review.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Future direction of corneal transplantation with new and innovative options for keratoconus and ectasia: descriptive review.
content.abstract: Recent advancements in the treatment of keratoconus and ectasia indicate a new era in managing these conditions, with promising innovations aimed at delaying or potentially preventing the need for invasive corneal transplantation. This review evaluates contemporary treatment modalities by analyzing recent literature on innovative techniques including corneal allogenic intrastromal ring segment insertion using both surgeon-prepared and technician-prepared donor corneas; lenticular insertion techniques such as implantation of keratorefractive lenticule extraction and xenograft implants, and Bowman layer transplantation. A comprehensive review of 132 articles published between January 2017 and April 2024 was conducted. This review aims to elucidate these emerging techniques for better understanding and adoption, providing detailed descriptions and assessing clinical outcomes and complications associated with each approach. By consolidating current knowledge, this review seeks to guide clinicians in selecting appropriate interventions and optimizing patient care for those affected by keratoconus and ectasia.

records.title: Suprachoroidal Drug Delivery for VEGF Suppression in Wet AMD and Other Diseases With Choroidal Neovascularization.

content.title: Suprachoroidal Drug Delivery for VEGF Suppression in Wet AMD and Other Diseases With Choroidal Neovascularization.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Choroidal neovascularization caused by age-related macular degeneration, among other diseases, causes significant visual impairment. Intravitreal therapeutics inhibiting vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) signaling have shown excellent safety and efficacy in regressing choroidal neovascularization and improving vision. Current US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved treatments deliver these drugs into the vitreous cavity, even though choroidal neovascularization originates from aberrant signaling in the choroid.

Design

Systematic review.

Methods

A literature search was conducted across PubMed and Google Scholar from inception up to December 31, 2024, focusing on studies investigating suprachoroidal delivery of anti-VEGF therapy. Randomized controlled trials, cohort studies, and case-control studies were included, whereas case reports and review articles were excluded.

Results

A total of 15 peer-reviewed articles, 3 press releases, 6 conference abstracts and presentations, and 8 clinical trials were identified that were relevant to the topic of suprachoroidal delivery of anti-VEGF therapy.

Conclusions

The suprachoroidal space is a potential space between the sclera and the choroid, which has recently become a route of delivery in an FDA-approved treatment. Notably, suprachoroidal delivery results in higher choroidal drug concentrations than intravitreal delivery. Promising results thus far have been seen with suprachoroidal delivery of VEGF-targeting therapies in clinical and preclinical studies; however, future work is needed to more fully demonstrate safety and efficacy.

records.title: Current Practices, Evolving Techniques, and Immunologic Challenges in Living and Deceased Donor Limbal Stem Cell Transplantation.

content.title: Current Practices, Evolving Techniques, and Immunologic Challenges in Living and Deceased Donor Limbal Stem Cell Transplantation.
content.abstract: This review focuses on allogeneic sources for restoring the ocular surface using limbal stem cell transplantation. We outline the current practices, evolving techniques, and immunologic challenges in living-related and deceased donor limbal stem cell transplantation. The diagnosis and staging guidelines for limbal stem cell deficiency are reviewed. We also explore the currently available treatment approaches, including the Cincinnati protocol for donor/recipient selection criteria and systemic immunosuppression (SI) regimen. Utilization of panel reactive antibody, HLA typing, ABO typing, and donor specific antibodies are highlighted. The traditional techniques as well as more novel variations are described. The importance of 3-agent SI protocols and patient adherence are emphasized to ensure excellent long-term outcomes. The primary immunologic challenge of allogeneic limbal stem cell transplantation, rejection, is also discussed in detail with recommended treatments, including a newer role for intravenous immunoglobulin. Other evolving practices have included a greater reliance on living-related conjunctival limbal allograft over deceased donor keratolimbal allograft due to improved outcomes, decreasing SI in older populations, and lengthening SI regimens due to the possibility of late acute rejection. Finally, we discuss the future of restoring the ocular surface via cell-based therapies, which may have the potential to decrease rejection.

records.title: Comparison of Femtosecond Laser Assistance and Manual Trephination in Deep Anterior Lamellar Keratoplasty in the Treatment of Keratoconus: A Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Comparison of Femtosecond Laser Assistance and Manual Trephination in Deep Anterior Lamellar Keratoplasty in the Treatment of Keratoconus: A Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare the efficacy and safety of femtosecond laser-assisted deep anterior lamellar keratoplasty (F-DALK) with those of manual-trephination DALK (M-DALK) in treating keratoconus.

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis.

Methods

Through November 2022, we comprehensively searched PubMed, EMBASE, the Cochrane Library, and 4 Chinese databases. Studies that involved comparisons between F-DALK and M-DALK groups and that reported on relevant efficacy and/or safety parameters were included. Primary outcomes were uncorrected- and corrected-distance visual acuity and intraoperative complication rates. Secondary outcomes were spherical equivalent, topographic astigmatism, refractive cylinder, mean keratometry, endothelial cell density, suture removal time, and postoperative complication rates. These data were analyzed using Cochrane Review Manager software version 5.3.

Results

This meta-analysis included 9 nonrandomized controlled studies involving 1713 eyes. In eyes treated with F-DALK, corrected-distance visual acuity at 1 to 6 months (weighted mean difference = -0.07 [95% confidence interval {CI} -0.10 to -0.03]; I2 = 0%; P < .001) after surgery was better and intraoperative Descemet membrane perforation occurred less often (odds ratio = 0.53 [95% CI 0.31-0.92]; I2 = 6%; P = .02) than in eyes treated with M-DALK. No clinically significant differences in other outcomes were found among the groups.

Conclusions

Both F-DALK and M-DALK are safe and efficacious for patients with keratoconus. Compared with M-DALK, F-DALK can provide better early visual acuity and reduce the intraoperative perforation rate, and its likely improvements to long-term visual quality and endothelial cell preservation warrant further investigation. In addition, the 2 techniques seem to be comparable regarding refractive outcomes and other complications.

records.title: Clinical and histological aspects of the anatomy of myopia, myopic macular degeneration and myopia-associated optic neuropathy.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Clinical and histological aspects of the anatomy of myopia, myopic macular degeneration and myopia-associated optic neuropathy.
content.abstract: Axial myopia is characterized by a panoply of morphological, clinical and histological, features in association with longer axial length. It includes changes in the region peripheral to the optic nerve head (reduction in the density of photoreceptors and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) cells and retinal thinning); in the optic nerve head region in moderately myopic eyes (shift of Bruch's membrane (BM) opening typically in the temporal/inferior direction, leading to a secondary BM overhang into the nasal intrapapillary compartment, BM absence in the temporal parapapillary region ("gamma zone"), and optic disc ovalization due to shortening of the ophthalmoscopically visible horizontal disc diameter; and widening of the RPE opening leading to myopic parapapillary beta zone), and in highly myopic eyes (BM opening enlargement resulting in a circular gamma zone, elongation and thinning of the lamina cribrosa ("secondary macrodisc") and of the peripapillary scleral flange ("parapapillary delta zone"); and in the macular region with an elongation of the fovea-optic disc distance, reduction in angle kappa, straightening/stretching of the papillomacular retinal blood vessels and retinal nerve fibers (leading to a re-arrangement of the retinal nerve fibers with a myopia-specific regional distribution of the retinal nerve fiber layer thickness profile), choroidal thinning most pronounced at the posterior pole and affecting mainly the medium-sized and large choroidal vessel layer), and scleral thinning. Pathologic changes in the macular region are extrafoveally located, linear RPE layer defects (lacquer cracks), potentially widening to round RPE layer defects (patchy atrophies), in some eyes with central BM defects; BM defects with RPE layer defects in the foveal region, accompanied by macular neovascularization or subsequent subretinal RPE cell proliferation ("macular atrophy"); myopic macular retinoschisis; and staphylomas. With longer axial length, the prevalence of non-glaucomatous optic neuropathy and glaucoma-like/glaucomatous optic neuropathy steeply increases beyond an axial length of 26.0-26.5 mm. With BM thickness being independent of axial length and in view of eye shape change from an oblate or sphere in emmetropia to a prolate rotational ellipsoid in myopia, the myopia specific morphological changes may be associated with a primary BM enlargement in the region peripheral to the optic disc.

records.title: International consensuses and controversies on causes, diagnosis and management of diabetic macular edema (DME).
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: International consensuses and controversies on causes, diagnosis and management of diabetic macular edema (DME).
content.abstract: Diabetic macular edema (DME) is the most common cause of vision-threatening diabetic retinopathy (VTDR) with an increasing prevalence tied to the global epidemic in diabetes. Despite significant advances, the management of DME remains a dynamic field with many unresolved controversies. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) allows objective assessment, however, correlation between vision and morphological changes can be inconsistent, causing disagreements on treatment strategies. DME is a complex disease with multifactorial pathophysiological pathways, leading to heterogenous treatment responses. There is a lack of standardized definition of treatment "non-response" and protocol for switching to second-line or adjuvant treatments. New anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) drugs and multi-targeted therapies seem to demonstrate improved durability, but long-term data is not yet available. Research in artificial intelligence (AI) is developing rapidly, however, rigorous appraisal of its reliability and generalizability are necessary before its implementation. Significant vision loss from DME in pregnant women, young children and elderly patients with systemic comorbidities are challenging conundrums. An international panel of experts (IPE) comprising 36 experts from 16 countries formulated and voted on the consensus statements in 5 key areas: 1) Diagnostic controversies around classification and imaging; 2) Treatment controversies; 3) Management paradigm between protocol-based and individualized approaches; 4) Emerging controversies in novel therapeutics and AI application, and 5) Special considerations for specific patient populations. There is an imminent need for mutual agreement on the best-possible approach to DME management in order to promote the optimal patient outcomes and to identify specific issues that require prioritization of resources and research.

records.title: Clinical histopathology and pathogenesis of macular telangiectasia type 2.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Clinical histopathology and pathogenesis of macular telangiectasia type 2.
content.abstract: Macular telangiectasia type 2 (MacTel) is a rare neurodegenerative retinal disease defined by a unique combination of reduced macular pigment, a characteristic angiographic pattern, and a localized clinical presentation. The condition typically affects the temporal perifovea and leads to progressive visual impairment. No definitive treatment exists. Current management is limited to intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) injections for end-stage neovascular complications and the recently approved Encelto implant (Neurotech Pharmaceuticals, Inc.), which delivers ciliary neurotrophic factor (CNTF) for neuroprotection. To clarify the still enigmatic pathophysiology of MacTel, we conducted a comprehensive review of all human histopathology reports published in English through December 31, 2024. Findings were systematically evaluated with respect to tissue processing techniques, postmortem fixation times, disease stage at last recorded ophthalmologic evaluation, diagnostic certainty, inclusion of control specimens, and the anatomic origin of analyzed retinal sections. This approach aimed to identify histopathologic features most likely to represent core disease mechanisms. Each of the features identified as most likely to be pathophysiologically relevant was independently assessed for clinical and histopathologic specificity. These features were then further interpreted in the context of genetic, metabolic, and anatomic associations reported in the literature. Donor demographics, coexisting ocular conditions, and systemic comorbidities were also reviewed to support the development of an integrative hypothesis for MacTel pathogenesis. Drawing on this synthesis, we propose a histopathology-informed model of disease pathophysiology and outline a provisional timeline for the contribution of key factors to clinical expression. We also review current neuroprotective strategies and provide targeted recommendations for future therapeutic development and histopathologic research. The conceptual framework developed in this work -grounded in rigorous analysis of the most consistent and methodologically validated histopathologic findings, and interpretation of their mechanistic context- may serve as a model for deciphering rare retinal diseases and for generating focused, hypothesis-driven questions to guide future investigation.

records.title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Automated Macular Hole Diagnosis and Structured Report Generation.

content.title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Automated Macular Hole Diagnosis and Structured Report Generation.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Current AI models for optical coherence tomography (OCT) primarily focus on diagnosis as a standalone task. We developed and validated an end-to-end agentic AI workflow that integrates automated macular hole (MH) diagnosis from OCT images with structured patient-friendly report generation.

Methods

The proposed sequential workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent consisted of an image diagnosis stage and a language generation step. The OCT version of RETFound, a self-supervised retinal foundation model, was fine-tuned for binary classification of macular OCT scans as MH or normal macula. Training, validation, and internal testing were performed using multiple public OCT datasets with patient-level stratified splitting, followed by external validation on two independent datasets. The performance of the fine-tuned foundation model was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC AUC). For each new OCT image, the AI agent used the trained RETFound model to classify the image, received the diagnostic output, incorporated it into a structured prompt, and called the large language model (GPT-4) to generate the clinical report.

Results

On the internal test set (n = 180), the model achieved an accuracy of 100% (95% confidence interval (CI), 97.9-100%) with an AUC of 1.00. On external validation (n = 1014), accuracy was 98.8% (95% CI 97.9-99.3%), sensitivity was 97.9% (95% CI 96.3-98.8%), specificity was 100% (95% CI 99.2-100.0%), and AUC was 0.999 (95% CI 0.998-1.000). Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) analysis showed that predictions were driven by relevant retinal regions, particularly the macular hole and adjacent layers. The end-to-end agentic AI workflow generated concise and standardized patient-friendly reports for all samples, without the language model influencing diagnostic decisions.

Conclusions

This study demonstrates the feasibility of an end-to-end AI workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent for robust OCT-based MH diagnosis with a large language model for structured report generation. By separating image-based diagnosis from language generation, this approach offers a practical and scalable solution for virtual vitreoretinal clinics.

records.title: The integral role of artificial intelligence models in retinal detachment diagnostics: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
records.publisher: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie

content.title: The integral role of artificial intelligence models in retinal detachment diagnostics: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Retinal detachment (RD) is a vision-threatening condition requiring prompt diagnosis and management to optimize visual outcomes. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models have demonstrated promising results in RD detection across multiple imaging modalities; however, concerns regarding heterogeneity, external validation, and real-world implementation remain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance and clinical applicability of AI models for RD diagnostics.

Methods

A comprehensive electronic search of PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), ClinicalTrials.gov, WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP), and Google Scholar was conducted in April 2026. Studies evaluating ML or DL models for RD detection, classification, segmentation, screening, or prognostic assessment using any imaging modality were included. Two independent reviewers performed study screening, data extraction, and quality assessment using the QUADAS-2 and CLAIM tools. Quantitative syntheses were performed using a bivariate random-effects model to pool sensitivity and specificity, while a random-effects inverse-variance model was applied for diagnostic odds ratio (DOR). Subgroup analyses were conducted according to imaging modality and use of external validation status. Publication bias and small-study effects were assessed using Deeks' funnel plot asymmetry test.

Results

Sixty-six studies were included in the systematic review, of which 31 studies comprising 118,432 images were eligible for meta-analysis. Fundus photography was the most commonly used imaging modality, and DL approaches predominated. The pooled sensitivity was 0.93 (95% CI: 0.89-0.95) and specificity was 0.98 (95% CI: 0.96-0.99), with moderate between-study heterogeneity. The model-based positive predictive value (PPV) and negative predictive value (NPV) were 0.86 (95% CI: 0.71-0.94) and 0.99 (95% CI: 0.97-1.00), respectively. The SROC curve yielded an AUC of 0.982 and a normalized pAUC of 0.964, while the pooled DOR was 642.3 (95% CI: 264.5-1559.7). No significant publication bias or small-study effects were detected (P = 0.544).

Conclusions

This study provides the most up-to-date comprehensive quantitative synthesis of AI applications for RD diagnostics, demonstrating excellent overall diagnostic performance across multiple imaging modalities. Despite these promising results, limited external and real-world clinical validation, together with methodological heterogeneity, continue to restrict clinical translation. Future multicenter prospective studies with standardized validation and reporting frameworks are essential for safe and generalizable implementation of AI-assisted RD diagnostics.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Laser-Assisted Refractive Surgery-A Comprehensive Review.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Laser-Assisted Refractive Surgery-A Comprehensive Review.
content.abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology-in the form of Machine Learning (ML) models and other models specialized in image recognition and processing, such as Convolutional Neural Networks Visual Transformers (CNN-ViTs)-is increasingly being used in ophthalmology. This review summarizes the main AI applications for laser-assisted refractive surgery. Methods: A wide-ranging literature search on the PubMed and ISI Thompson Web of Science databases was conducted. Results: AI is an all-encompassing technological concept that refers to either specific applications of ML/CNN models, such as in keratoconus screening or diagnosis, or agentic/multimodal AI applications that process different data types using a variety of AI models. The most clinically established applications found were corneal ectasia and keratoconus screening, in which AI models can reliably exceed 95% diagnostic accuracy, specificity, and sensitivity; nomogram-derived laser ablation programming; optimization of ray-tracing calculations for ray-traced ablation profiles; patient screening and selection for refractive surgery; visual and refractive result prediction; assessment of postoperative corneal ectasia risk; detection of intraoperative complications; research on the laser coupling effect; and other applications such as monitoring eye rubbing behavior in corneal ectasia suspects. Thus, singular, specific applications of AI models have made the largest clinical contributions. These results must be interpreted with a comparison of internal versus external validation, calibration, and generalizability. Overall the technology is highly promising. Agentic/multimodal AI frameworks are currently being discussed, with pilot studies published and applicability proposed in the context of large, high-patient-volume clinical practices. The technological advent of SHAP force plot graphs and saliency maps has improved understanding of the factors that contribute mechanistically to AI model reasoning, leading to more informed clinical decisions or research applicability, such as in finding parameters or factors linked to postoperative ectasia. Conclusions: AI is already established in laser-assisted refractive surgery in the form of models specialized in data-intensive analysis. At present, the best-performing novel AI models originate from the domain of large or multi-hospital settings due to requirements for multiple latest-generation diagnostic devices, high-volume patient data, computing expertise, and resources. Future directions could include clinical standardization and trickle-down dissemination of the technology. Agentic/multimodal AI has the potential to benefit large clinical/patient settings or offer access to expert knowledge in smaller practice settings. Agentic/multimodal AI implementation is offset by challenges in complexity, the technological limitations of LLMs ("hallucinations"), and ethical and legislative factors.

records.title: Deep Learning-Based Retinal Vascular Analysis with Quantitative Metrics for Hypertensive Microvascular Damage.

content.title: Deep Learning-Based Retinal Vascular Analysis with Quantitative Metrics for Hypertensive Microvascular Damage.
content.abstract: Background/Objectives: The goal of this study was to determine whether deep learning (DL)-assisted retinal vascular analysis detects subclinical microvascular remodeling associated with hypertension-mediated target organ damage (TOD) in patients with absent or mild hypertensive retinopathy (HR). Methods: This prospective study included age-comparable hypertensive patients with TOD (n = 54), hypertensive patients without TOD (n = 54), and healthy controls (n = 54). Color fundus photographs underwent DL-based segmentation using the Retinal Microvascular Health Assessment System, ophthalmologist quality review, and Fiji morphometric analysis. Central retinal arteriolar and venular equivalents (CRAE and CRVE), arteriovenous ratio (AVR), and arterial and venous network metrics were quantified. Results: AVR decreased progressively from 0.814 ± 0.038 in controls to 0.740 ± 0.043 in hypertensive patients without TOD and 0.655 ± 0.042 in those with TOD (p < 0.001). CRAE and CRVE differed among groups (p < 0.001 and p = 0.002). Arterial fractal dimension and vessel area density (VAD) declined stepwise (both p < 0.001), whereas arterial skeletonized vascular density (SVD) and diameter were primarily reduced in TOD. Venous VAD and diameter differed (p = 0.022 and p = 0.006), but venous SVD did not (p = 0.146). After adjustment among hypertensive participants, TOD remained associated with lower AVR, CRAE, and all arterial network metrics except tortuosity (all p < 0.001), but not with venous parameters. Conclusions: Retinal arterial alterations were associated with established extra-retinal TOD in patients with absent or mild HR. Residual cardiovascular confounding limits interpretation, and longitudinal studies are needed to establish temporal relationships, predictive value, and clinical utility.

records.title: Modeling distinct pathogenesis of early- and late-onset preeclampsia via hierarchical representation learning of interactome.

content.title: Modeling distinct pathogenesis of early- and late-onset preeclampsia via hierarchical representation learning of interactome.
content.abstract:
Objectives

We developed and validated the pathogenesis models by hierarchical representation learning of interactomes connecting endometrial maturation, placentation, chorioamnionitis, and hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme, and low platelet (HELLP) syndrome.

Methods

We utilized 19 gene sets from our previous work to infer interactomes to develop (n = 177) and validate (n = 352) explainable artificial intelligence models for each preeclampsia subtype using deep-insight visible neural network, gradient-weighted class activation mapping, and large language model.

Results

The hierarchically learned representations identified novel genes for late-onset preeclampsia (LOPE), similar to chorioamnionitis (ANKRD13A, SLA), and HELLP syndrome (PDE5A). We also identified novel genes for early-onset preeclampsia (EOPE), similar to HELLP syndrome (SWAP70, GREM2, GPR146, PIP5K1B, EZR).

Conclusions

Our pathogenesis models connected HELLP syndrome with both LOPE and EOPE. However, chorioamnionitis was only connected with LOPE.

records.title: The association between large language model dependence and academic anxiety among nursing students: statistical indirect associations through artificial intelligence addiction and academic burnout.

content.title: The association between large language model dependence and academic anxiety among nursing students: statistical indirect associations through artificial intelligence addiction and academic burnout.
content.abstract:
Background

Increasing use of large language models in nursing education has raised questions about the association between reliance on these tools and academic distress. This study examined direct and specific indirect associations between large language model dependence (LMD) and academic anxiety (AA) through artificial intelligence addiction (AIA) and academic burnout (AB).

Methods

A cross-sectional survey was conducted from March to April 2026 among 473 nursing students in Guangdong Province, China, including students undertaking clinical placements. The four constructs were assessed using items selected from published self-report instruments. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was performed with age and sex included as covariates. Direct and specific indirect associations were evaluated using bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples.

Results

Cronbach's α ranged from 0.914 to 0.944, composite reliability from 0.935 to 0.954, and average variance extracted from 0.560 to 0.721. Heterotrait-monotrait ratios ranged from 0.485 to 0.733, supporting discriminant validity. Model fit evidence was mixed: SRMR was 0.068, whereas NFI was 0.812, below the 0.90 reference value. The model explained 49.2% of the variance in academic anxiety. Large language model dependence showed a small positive direct association with academic anxiety (β = 0.138, 95% CI [0.006, 0.278], p = 0.048). Significant specific indirect associations were identified through academic burnout (β = 0.205, 95% CI [0.123, 0.303]) and through artificial intelligence addiction followed by academic burnout (β = 0.098, 95% CI [0.049, 0.147]); both p < 0.001.

Conclusion

Large language model dependence was positively associated with academic anxiety among nursing students, with specific indirect associations through academic burnout and through artificial intelligence addiction followed by academic burnout. These findings highlight the relevance of problematic AI use and study-related exhaustion to academic distress. However, the cross-sectional design does not establish temporal ordering or causal mediation.

records.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.

content.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.
content.abstract:
Aims

Whether a retinal artificial intelligence (AI) risk score reclassifies SCORE2 cardiovascular risk stratification in statin-naive adults across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary is uncertain. We evaluated the retinal AI risk score for 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) prediction.

Methods

In 40,672 statin-naive UK Biobank participants (aged 40-69, without diabetes), cardiovascular risk categories and treatment recommendation status (Class I or IIa vs neither) were defined using the 2025 ESC/EAS focused-update framework. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) adjusted for SCORE2 or for established risk factors. The incremental predictive value of adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation.

Results

Over a 10.0-year median follow-up (914 ASCVD events), the very high retinal AI risk group independently predicted ASCVD (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.32 vs low risk; p<0.001). Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 reclassified risk across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary (statin-eligibility NRI [net reclassification improvement] 0.012, p<0.001); reclassification was statistically significant but modest (continuous NRI 0.445, p<0.001), without C-index or net-benefit gain. In the statin-indicated subgroup, retinal AI risk groups further stratified risk (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.16; p<0.001). Statin-not-indicated participants in the high or very high retinal AI risk groups had numerically similar observed 10-year risk to all statin-indicated, untreated participants (p=0.758). There was no evidence of effect modification by clinically detectable retinal disorder (interaction p=0.93). Incremental value was greater in women than men (sex interaction p<0.001).

Conclusion

Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 produced modest bidirectional risk reclassification across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary; these findings warrant prospective validation.Abstract word count: 250 words.

records.title: Deep Learning-Based Automated Detection, Segmentation, and Quantification of Retinal Fluid on Optical Coherence Tomography: A Validation Study.

content.title: Deep Learning-Based Automated Detection, Segmentation, and Quantification of Retinal Fluid on Optical Coherence Tomography: A Validation Study.
content.abstract: Objectives: To validate a deep learning-based algorithm for automated detection, segmentation, and quantitative assessment of retinal fluid on optical coherence tomography (OCT) across multiple retinal diseases. Methods: In this retrospective validation study, spectral-domain OCT volume scans from eyes with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), diabetic macular edema (DME), and macular telangiectasia type 2 (MacTel) were analyzed. Automated segmentation was performed using the fluid analyzer on Skopix by NetraMind Innovations, a deep learning-based framework trained to identify intraretinal fluid (IRF), subretinal fluid (SRF), pigment epithelial detachment (PED), and subretinal hyperreflective material (SHRM). Automated segmentations were reviewed and manually corrected by two masked experienced retina graders, with discrepancies adjudicated by a senior retina specialist. Scan-level detection performance was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and Gwet's first-order agreement coefficient (AC1). Spatial segmentation agreement across all B-scans was assessed using the Dice coefficient. Quantitative agreement between automated and manually corrected fluid volumes was evaluated using correlation and Bland-Altman analyses. Inter-grader reliability was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Results: A total of 98 OCT volumes comprising 31 nAMD, 25 DME, and 42 MacTel eyes were included. In nAMD, IRF detection demonstrated a sensitivity of 81.8%, specificity of 83.0%, and AUC of 0.876, while SRF demonstrated a sensitivity of 81.4%, specificity of 96.7%, and AUC of 0.901. In DME, sensitivity, specificity, and AUC were 99.6%, 97.3%, and 0.989 for IRF and 98.4%, 96.4%, and 0.978 for SRF, respectively. In MacTel, IRF demonstrated a sensitivity of 87.3%, specificity of 95.1%, and AUC of 0.927, while SRF demonstrated a sensitivity of 86.8%, specificity of 98.4%, and AUC of 0.929. Segmentation agreement between automated and manually corrected annotations was high across disease groups, with Dice coefficients of 0.829 and 0.922 for IRF and SRF in nAMD, 0.858 and 0.941 in DME, and 0.908 and 0.97 in MacTel, respectively. Automated fluid volumes demonstrated strong correlations with manually corrected measurements, with minimal systematic bias on Bland-Altman analysis. Conclusions: The automated segmentation algorithm demonstrated strong validation performance for the detection and quantitative assessment of retinal fluid across nAMD, DME, and MacTel. High segmentation agreement, particularly for IRF and SRF, and strong volumetric agreement with expert-corrected measurements support the potential use of automated OCT fluid quantification in clinical practice and research.

records.title: Association between deep-learning-derived retinal aging speed and rapid decline of renal function in the Japanese general population.

content.title: Association between deep-learning-derived retinal aging speed and rapid decline of renal function in the Japanese general population.
content.abstract:
Background

The eye and the kidney share microvascular features, and retinal changes have been postulated to reflect systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction. Recently, retinal age, estimated by deep learning (DL) from a single fundus photograph, has been shown to predict cardiovascular events. The present study aimed to determine whether retinal aging speed, defined as the individual-specific annual rate of change in DL-estimated retinal age, is associated with rapid estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decline.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed the longitudinal data obtained from 7807 Japanese individuals who underwent repeated health check-ups with serial measurements of eGFR and fundus photographs (median 9.0 visits over median 8.0 years). We evaluated the relationship between retinal aging speed during the baseline period (from baseline to year 4) and rapid eGFR decline (≤ -3 ml/min/1.73 m²/year) during the follow-up period (after year 4).

Results

The incidence of rapid eGFR decline was significantly higher in the highest quartile of retinal aging speed than in the lowest quartile as the reference group in the fully adjusted model adjusting age, sex, body mass index, blood pressure, diabetes, smoking, eGFR, and proteinuria [odds ratio (OR) 1.34; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.06-1.68; P = .015]. In the multivariable logistic regression models, retinal aging speed was associated with rapid eGFR decline after adjusting multiple key confounders (OR 1.14; 95% CI 1.02-1.29; P = .027).

Conclusions

Taken together, DL-derived retinal aging speed is independently associated with rapid eGFR decline in the Japanese general population.

records.title: Tumor Budding in Colorectal Cancer: Biological Basis, Clinical Risk Stratification, and Digital Pathology.

content.title: Tumor Budding in Colorectal Cancer: Biological Basis, Clinical Risk Stratification, and Digital Pathology.
content.abstract: Tumor budding, defined as single tumor cells or clusters of up to four cells at the invasive front, is a morphological marker of tumor-cell dissociation and stromal invasion in colorectal cancer. Standardization by the International Tumor Budding Consensus Conference (ITBCC) established a reproducible hematoxylin-and-eosin-based method and enabled broader incorporation of budding into pathology reporting and clinical risk assessment. Intermediate- and high-grade budding are associated with lymph node metastasis in pT1 colorectal cancer, while high-grade budding identifies a subgroup of stage II colon cancers with increased recurrence risk. Adverse prognostic associations have also been reported in stage III disease and in rectal cancer after neoadjuvant therapy, although evidence that budding predicts benefit from a specific treatment is still insufficient. At the biological level, budding is linked to partial epithelial-mesenchymal transition, altered cell adhesion, cytoskeletal remodeling, and interactions with fibroblasts, extracellular matrix, and immune cells. Digital pathology and artificial intelligence may improve hotspot selection, quantification, and spatial characterization, but their clinical use depends on external validation, control of domain shift, and continued pathologist oversight. Tumor budding is therefore best interpreted as a complementary morphological biomarker alongside TNM stage, established histopathological risk factors, molecular features, and clinical context.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Valvular Heart Disease: Imaging, Quantification, Risk Prediction, and Potential Clinical Decision Support.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Valvular Heart Disease: Imaging, Quantification, Risk Prediction, and Potential Clinical Decision Support.
content.abstract: Valvular heart disease (VHD) affects a substantial proportion of the population and remains a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality worldwide. Despite advances in surgical and transcatheter therapies, important challenges persist. VHD remains underdiagnosed, assessment of disease severity is often variable, and the optimal timing of intervention continues to evolve. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool across the spectrum of VHD care. AI-based electrocardiogram analysis can identify both existing and future VHD, while AI-guided point-of-care ultrasound extends screening to nonspecialist settings. Across multimodality imaging, machine learning (ML) and deep learning algorithms enable automated, reproducible assessment of VHD. In echocardiography, AI supports grading of disease severity across the main valvular lesions, including Doppler interpretation and automated report generation. AI-enhanced cardiac magnetic resonance facilitates automated assessment of ventricular remodeling and myocardial fibrosis, while AI-assisted cardiac computed tomography improves procedural planning for transcatheter interventions. In parallel, ML has identified distinct patient phenotypes in multiple valvular lesions with differing clinical trajectories and responses to intervention. This review summarizes current applications of AI in detection, multimodality imaging, and potential clinical decision support for VHD and discusses opportunities and challenges for integration into routine practice.

records.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.

content.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Echocardiography has evolved substantially since its introduction in 1954. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers transformative potential for image acquisition, quantification, interpretation, and reporting. Despite growing research interest, a comprehensive evaluation of the historical trends and evolution of AI in echocardiography is lacking. The study aimed to conduct a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of the global research landscape in this field.

Methods

A systematic literature search was conducted using the Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection databases for publications on AI in echocardiography from inception through November 10, 2025; no language filter was applied. Data analysis was performed using Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Access, and IBM SPSS Statistics. In addition, bibliometric mapping and data visualization were conducted.

Results

Overall, 2682 publications received 35,083 citations (mean, 13.08 citations per publication), spanning 1984-2025. Original articles, conference papers, and review articles accounted for 87.4% and 98.5% of total publications and citations, respectively. Publication output remained limited until approximately 2015, rose gradually thereafter, and accelerated markedly after 2018, with similar output in 2024 and 2025. The United States led in both publication volume and total citations, followed by China and the United Kingdom. The United States also had the highest collaboration link strength, and seven of the top 10 institutions were in North America (six in the United States and one in Canada). Mayo Clinic ranked first, with 142 publications and 3604 citations, and had the earliest first indexed publication among the top institutions (1992). The journal JACC: Cardiovascular Imaging ranked first in both total citations (1,911) and citations per publication (36.75). "Echocardiography," "deep learning," "artificial intelligence," and "machine learning" were the most frequently used terms. The thematic evolution showed continuity of algorithmic-centric themes (1984-2019) with emerging clinically oriented themes (2020-2025).

Conclusions

This comprehensive bibliometric analysis highlights the rapid expansion of AI research in echocardiography, characterized by an accelerating publication output and emerging clinically oriented research topics. These findings reflect growing research interest in integrating AI into echocardiographic practice and highlight the need for future research prioritizing multicenter validation, clinical translation, and equitable real-world implementation.

records.title: Empirical Evaluation of Post Hoc Interpretability Methods for Clinical Trust in Deep Learning Diagnostics.

content.title: Empirical Evaluation of Post Hoc Interpretability Methods for Clinical Trust in Deep Learning Diagnostics.
content.abstract: Background/Objectives: Brain tumor classification from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has been significantly improved through deep learning techniques; however, the lack of interpretability remains a major challenge for clinical adoption. Methods: This study proposes an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-driven framework for multiclass brain tumor classification using a baseline convolutional neural network (CNN) and four transfer learning models, namely ResNet50, DenseNet121, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNetB0. The models were trained and evaluated on a publicly available brain MRI dataset consisting of glioma, meningioma, and pituitary tumor classes. Their classification performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC), and confusion matrix analysis. To enhance transparency and interpretability, Grad-CAM, LIME, and SHAP were used to visualize and quantify the regions contributing to the classification decisions. Results: Experimental results state that the transfer learning models consistently outperformed the CNN by learning more discriminative feature representations while producing more localized and interpretable explanations. The agreement among Grad-CAM, LIME, and SHAP confirms that the proposed models predominantly relied on tumor regions rather than irrelevant background information, thereby improving the interpretability and reliability of the diagnostic predictions. Conclusions: The proposed framework provides an effective and explainable computer-aided diagnosis system that supports trustworthy deep learning-based brain tumor classification and has the potential for decision-making.

records.title: Impact of Image Bit Depth Reduction on Deep Learning Performance in Chest Radiograph Analysis: A Multi-institutional Study.

content.title: Impact of Image Bit Depth Reduction on Deep Learning Performance in Chest Radiograph Analysis: A Multi-institutional Study.
content.abstract:
Rationale and objectives

Medical imaging typically generates 12-bit to 16-bit formats, yet conversion to 8-bit is often required. While deep learning has been widely explored in medical imaging, the influence of image bit depth on model performance is not fully understood. This study evaluates the impact of conversion from 16-bit to 8-bit for sex, age, and obesity classification using deep learning.

Materials and methods

In this retrospective, multi-institutional study, we analyzed 100,002 chest radiographs from 48,047 participants across three institutions. Images were uniformly quantized from the fixed 0-65535 range to 256 levels (0-255) with no additional processing. Three convolutional neural network architectures (ResNet52, EfficientNetB2, and ConvNeXtSmall) were trained on both 16-bit and 8-bit versions of the images. Model performance was evaluated using internal test datasets, randomly split multiple times, and an external test dataset. Statistical analysis included paired comparisons of area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) values, with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons.

Results

Across all architectures and classification tasks, differences between 16-bit and 8-bit model performance were minimal (mean differences ranging from -0.218%-0.184%). Statistical analyses revealed no significant differences in AUC-ROC values between bit depths for any model-task combination (all p values > 0.05 after Bonferroni correction). Effect sizes were small to moderate (Cohen's d ranging from -0.415-0.391).

Conclusion

No statistically significant differences were detected between models trained on 16-bit and 8-bit images in the three evaluated tasks. These findings suggest that conversion to 8-bit images may reduce data storage requirements and improve data processing efficiency. Further research is needed to assess their usefulness in clinical tasks.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.
content.abstract:
Background

Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy in women globally, accounting for approximately 2.30 million new cases and 666,103 deaths in 2022. Artificial intelligence technologies including machine learning, deep learning, radiomics, and natural language processing have been widely applied across the breast cancer care continuum. However, no systematic review restricted to primary studies with patient-level or image-level data has synthesized evidence spanning all clinical domains simultaneously.

Objectives

To evaluate the performance, methodological quality, and clinical relevance of artificial intelligence primary studies across screening and diagnostic imaging, digital pathology, radiomics, perioperative management, prognostic prediction, and natural language processing in breast cancer.

Methods

PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2015 to May 2026. Eligibility was restricted to original primary research reporting patient-level or image-level data; secondary syntheses were explicitly excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 and PROBAST. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

Results

Of 5,275 identified records, 17 primary studies met eligibility criteria. In screening mammography (seven studies; n = 7,540 to 144,231 examinations), deep learning achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.876 to 0.939; a randomised trial in 80,033 women demonstrated non-inferiority to double reading with a 44.3% reduction in radiologist workload. In digital pathology (five studies; 270 to 44,732 whole-slide images), deep learning achieved AUC 0.985 to 0.994, exceeding unassisted pathologist performance in lymph node metastasis detection. Magnetic resonance imaging radiomics predicted pathological complete response in HER2-positive breast cancer with AUC 0.80. No breast cancer-specific perioperative primary study met the eligibility criteria. Deep survival networks achieved concordance index 0.626 versus 0.612 for Cox regression in breast cancer cohorts. Natural language processing identified metastatic recurrence in breast cancer clinical records with sensitivity 83% and specificity 73%. Risk of bias was low to moderate for imaging and pathology studies and high for small sample radiomics studies. Density-stratified performance was reported by only two imaging studies, and receptor status prediction from haematoxylin and eosin staining had not been validated as a safe alternative to immunohistochemistry.

Conclusions

Artificial intelligence demonstrated clinically meaningful performance across the five domains with eligible primary studies. Breast cancer-specific perioperative and intensive care primary studies were absent, representing the largest evidence gap. External validation, demographic diversity, and prospective clinical integration evidence remained the most consistently identified limitations. Prediction of molecular receptor status without immunohistochemistry requires rigorous prospective safety validation before it can complement standard testing.

records.title: Toward Clinically Trustworthy Deep Learning in Cardiology: A Unified Mathematical Synthesis of Representation, Optimization, and Reliability.

content.title: Toward Clinically Trustworthy Deep Learning in Cardiology: A Unified Mathematical Synthesis of Representation, Optimization, and Reliability.
content.abstract: Background: Deep learning (DL) has revolutionized cardiovascular medicine by allowing for automated analysis of electrocardiography, imaging of the heart, and multimodal clinical datasets. Although there have been impressive advancements in terms of predictive performance, the deployment of DL methods in a clinical setting remains limited due to lack of sufficient mathematical understanding around the concepts of uncertainty, robustness, fairness, explainability, and generalizability. Methods: In this work, a systematic review is conducted using PRISMA principles on 79 peer-reviewed articles published from 2017 until 2025, with a unifying mathematical perspective on the notion of trustworthy deep learning in cardiology. Results: We find that there is significant discrepancy between prediction accuracy and clinical reliability, with little emphasis placed on mathematical guarantees, reproducibility of evaluation procedures, calibration, or robustness verification. To address this challenge, we propose a conceptual mathematical framework which brings together the elements of representation learning, optimization, and trustworthiness into a unified audit of AI in cardiac care. We note that the presented indices are purely theoretical and are meant to provide guidance for future standardization, and as such do not represent actual clinical metrics. Conclusions: Although our paper does not propose any new predictive algorithms, we do contribute a strong theoretical basis for the evaluation and development of clinically reliable deep learning algorithms in cardiology.

records.title: Digital twin oncology and multi-omics-driven artificial intelligence models for personalized drug response prediction: A systematic survey of emerging computational paradigms and clinical implementation challenges.

content.title: Digital twin oncology and multi-omics-driven artificial intelligence models for personalized drug response prediction: A systematic survey of emerging computational paradigms and clinical implementation challenges.
content.abstract: The increasing complexity of tumor heterogeneity and variable therapeutic response has intensified the need for accurate personalized drug response prediction in oncology. Traditional trial-and-error chemotherapy strategies often result in suboptimal outcomes, toxicity, and delayed therapeutic adjustments. Rapid advances in multi-omics technologies, artificial intelligence (AI) and digital twin modeling have significantly reshaped computational oncology research. This survey systematically reviews peer-reviewed research and review articles published from 2021 onward that investigate emerging computational paradigms integrating digital twins and multi-omics AI for drug response prediction. The foundational concepts in digital twin oncology, multi-omics profiling and AI-driven precision medicine are outlined initially. The existing approaches are categorized into four major paradigms such as omics-driven machine learning models, deep learning based multimodal architectures, mechanistic digital twin simulation frameworks and hybrid digital twin AI systems enabling adaptive therapy optimization. The multi-omics data integration strategies, including early, intermediate, late, network-based and graph/pathway-based fusion techniques. The survey synthesizes recent developments in drug sensitivity prediction, immunotherapy response modeling, tumor evolution forecasting and virtual clinical trials, while critically analyzing challenges related to data heterogeneity, interpretability, generalization, privacy, regulatory compliance and ethical considerations. Finally, future directions are highlighted such as real-time adaptive digital twins, federated learning, explainable AI and regulatory ready clinical deployment frameworks. Overall, this review provides a structured taxonomy, comparative analysis and research roadmap for advancing integrated digital twin and multi omics AI systems toward clinically actionable precision oncology.

records.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.

content.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), especially the recent proliferation of generative Large Language Models (LLMs), is transforming traditional anatomy education by introducing new teaching tools. However, the adoption of these cutting-edge technologies raises questions about global educational equity. It remains unclear whether AI will serve as a digital equalizer or further exacerbate marginalization. This rapid bibliometric synthesis aims to provide a comprehensive, data-driven overview of the "Application of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education" (AAAE). We seek to map the intellectual landscape, detect structural and technological shifts, evaluate the geopolitical disparities, and provide corresponding references. A total of 85 consolidated records were retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus. These data constituted the whole panorama of AAAE. Bibliometrix and CiteSpace were utilized for static and dynamic mapping. A multidisciplinary expert panel validated the thematic clusters using Gwet's AC1 and the Normalized Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI). Publications surged following ChatGPT's release, indicating a shift from specialized computer vision to the application of general-purpose LLMs. While high-income countries maintain leadership, AI could exert a "democratizing effect" on upper-middle-income countries, doubling their odds of publication compared to traditional anatomy. Six research frontiers and three research trajectories were captured, and corresponding implications for future researchers in the global south and north were presented. AAAE could be conducted using a stratified strategy: different expansions of AI technologies for pedagogy; leveraging commercial APIs to bypass infrastructure bottlenecks; and validating open-source models. Global equity critically demands cross-border collaboration and inclusive datasets.

records.title: Artificial intelligence analysis of oral mucosal lesions in white-light clinical photographs: A systematic review of visual features and validation.

content.title: Artificial intelligence analysis of oral mucosal lesions in white-light clinical photographs: A systematic review of visual features and validation.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to conventional oral photographs for recognition, classification, localization, segmentation, and risk assessment of oral mucosal lesions. This systematic review evaluated how clinically relevant visual information-including color, texture, morphology, borders, and spatial patterns-is represented by AI systems and assessed performance, validation, explainability, human comparison, and clinical translation. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for studies directly analyzing conventional white-light clinical photographs. Risk of bias was assessed with PROBAST + AI, and certainty with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation-based approaches. Fifty-three studies were included, 30 published in 2025-2026. Forty-six used implicit deep-learning visual representations, three multimodal vision-language models, two explicit color analyses, and two explicit texture analyses. Thirty-one studies primarily addressed image-level diagnostic classification/recognition, 15 spatial detection/localization or lesion delineation, six screening/triage/referral or biopsy-oriented decision support, and one longitudinal malignant-transformation prediction. Six used independent external cohorts and five compared AI with human readers. Methodological concerns were frequent, no sufficiently coherent group supported meta-analysis, and certainty remained limited across evidence bodies. Current evidence therefore supports technical feasibility rather than established clinical effectiveness, with translation requiring stronger patient-level independence, external validation, prospective multicenter evaluation, and evidence of clinical benefit.
