This paper provides a comprehensive review of recent research on deep learning applications for radiotherapy dose prediction, highlighting the architectures, datasets, and methodologies used.

Results

The review highlights the advancements in accuracy, efficiency, and robustness achieved by deep learning-based dose prediction models. These approaches help reduce treatment planning time and minimize human error, thereby improving clinical workflows.

Conclusion

Deep learning offers promising solutions to enhance radiotherapy dose delivery. Future research should focus on developing the generalized dose prediction models, multi-institutional validation frameworks, explainable AI approaches for clinical trust, real-time adaptation capabilities, uncertainty quantification methods, and strategies for handling rare anatomical variations.

records.title: Research progress in agitation early warning monitoring and new technologies for critically ill patients: a narrative review.

content.title: Research progress in agitation early warning monitoring and new technologies for critically ill patients: a narrative review.
content.abstract: Agitation is a common and clinically significant problem in critically ill patients, closely associated with unplanned extubation, device removal, prolonged hospital stay, and increased mortality. Traditional assessment tools such as the richmond agitation-sedation scale (RASS) and sedation-agitation scale (SAS), despite their widespread use, are limited by intermittent assessment, subjectivity, and inability to provide continuous monitoring. In recent years, the rapid development of artificial intelligence and sensing technologies has opened new avenues for objective, continuous, and real-time agitation monitoring through vital sign-based parameters, video surveillance with computer vision, wearable devices, and multimodal fusion approaches. This narrative review systematically examines the epidemiological characteristics and clinical consequences of agitation in critically ill patients, analyzes the limitations of traditional assessment tools, and highlights emerging technologies based on physiological signals, computer vision, deep learning, and multimodal integration. The current status and challenges of agitation monitoring in various clinical settings-including intensive care units, emergency departments, prehospital environments, and inter-hospital transport-are discussed. Finally, future directions for multimodal early warning systems in complex environments are proposed, providing a theoretical foundation for constructing a comprehensive agitation monitoring system spanning prehospital, in-hospital, and transport settings based on vital signs and video-based behavioral analysis.

records.title: A systematic review on the generative AI applications in human medical genetics.

content.title: A systematic review on the generative AI applications in human medical genetics.
content.abstract: Although traditional statistical techniques and machine learning methods have contributed significantly to genetics and, in particular, inherited disease diagnosis, they often struggle with complex, high-dimensional data, a challenge now addressed by state-of-the-art deep learning models. Large language models (LLMs), based on transformer architectures, have excelled in tasks requiring contextual comprehension of unstructured medical data. This systematic review examines the role of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) methods in human medical genomics, focusing on the genetic research and diagnostics of both rare and common diseases. Automated keyword-based search in PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv, and arXiv was conducted, targeting studies on LLM applications in diagnostics and education within genetics and removing irrelevant or outdated models. A total of 195 studies were analyzed, highlighting the prospects of their applications in knowledge navigation, analysis of clinical and genetic data, and interaction with patients and medical professionals. Key findings indicate that while transformer-based models perform well across a diverse range of tasks (such as identification of tentative molecular diagnosis from clinical data or genetic variant interpretation), major challenges persist in integrating multimodal data (genomic sequences, imaging, and clinical records) into unified and clinically robust pipelines, facing limitations in generalizability and practical implementation in clinical settings. This review provides a comprehensive classification and assessment of the current capabilities and limitations of LLMs in transforming hereditary disease diagnostics and supporting genetic education, serving as a guide to navigate this rapidly evolving field, while outlining application use cases, implementation guidance, and forward-looking research directions.

records.title: Hyperbaric oxygen in the artificial intelligence era: integration and innovation.

content.title: Hyperbaric oxygen in the artificial intelligence era: integration and innovation.
content.abstract: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is established for decompression illness, carbon monoxide poisoning, radiation-induced tissue injury, and diabetic foot ulcers. Interest in neurological and inflammatory indications is growing, yet outcomes are constrained by heterogeneous protocols, limited patient selection tools, and the absence of real-time physiological guidance. Artificial intelligence, including machine learning, explainable artificial intelligence, and digital twins, has transformed other clinical domains and could enable precision hyperbaric oxygen therapy. We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar (January 2000-March 2025). Terms included "hyperbaric oxygen therapy" and ("artificial intelligence" OR "machine learning" OR "deep learning" OR "digital twin" OR "biosensor*"). English-language, peer-reviewed clinical, preclinical, or computational studies explicitly linking hyperbaric oxygen therapy with artificial intelligence or enabling technologies were eligible. Editorials without primary data, abstracts without full text, and non-peer-reviewed sources were excluded. A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses-style flow-guided screening and selection. Fifty-three eligible studies (≥30% from 2022-2025) illustrate four convergent application areas: (1) protocol optimization using multicenter data, (2) biomarker-driven patient selection via multi-omics and imaging, (3) real-time adaptive control using biosensors, and (4) predictive safety analytics for oxygen toxicity and barotrauma. Exemplars from radiology, critical care, and cardiology demonstrate the feasibility of decision support, federated learning, and digital-twin simulations adaptable to hyperbaric oxygen therapy. Integrating artificial intelligence with hyperbaric oxygen therapy can shift practice from empirical protocols to patient-tailored, data-informed therapy. Priorities include hybrid clinical trials, interoperable registries, explainable and bias-aware models, and regulatory-aligned validation. With rigorous governance, artificial intelligence can improve efficacy, safety, and efficiency while advancing mechanistic understanding of hyperbaric oxygen therapy.

records.title: Effects of different complementary therapies on chronic kidney disease-associated pruritus: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.

content.title: Effects of different complementary therapies on chronic kidney disease-associated pruritus: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Chronic kidney disease-associated pruritus is one of the most common concomitant symptoms in patients with end-stage renal disease. It leads to multiple adverse outcomes for patients. Complementary therapies are increasingly used and represent an effective alternative approach. However, the optimal intervention method has not yet been clearly established.

Objective

To compare the efficacy and safety of different complementary therapies in alleviating symptoms of chronic kidney disease-associated pruritus.

Methods

A systematic search was conducted in 12 databases and relevant medical websites in accordance with the PRISMA-NMA guidelines. Randomized controlled trials published in the database from database inception through December 2025 were included. The Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2.0) was used to assess the quality of the included literature. High-risk-of-bias studies were excluded and subsequently re-included in the sensitivity analysis. Statistical analysis was performed using Bayesian methods with the "gemtc" package and other R packages. The quality of evidence was assessed using the CINeMA online platform.

Results

A total of 29 studies involving 12 complementary and alternative approaches and 1,968 patients were included. The network meta-analysis showed that Acupuncture (SMD = -2.12, 95% CI = -4.17 to -0.13; SUCRA = 0.80), Aromatherapy (SMD = -2.05, 95% CI = -4.00 to -0.08; SUCRA = 0.78), Herbal Medicinal Bath (SMD = -1.69, 95% CI = -2.67 to -0.71; SUCRA = 0.72) and Combination therapy (SMD = -1.47, 95% CI = -2.53 to -0.43; SUCRA = 0.65) were superior to the control group in improving pruritus symptoms. However, when the 9 excluded high-risk-of-bias studies were re-included in a sensitivity analysis, the effects of Acupuncture and other therapies were attenuated and no longer statistically significant. Only Herbal Medicinal Bath maintained a statistically significant and stable effect (SMD = -2.40, 95% CI = -3.60 to -1.21; SUCRA = 0.82).

Conclusion

Based on the efficacy and stability of the current evidence, Herbal Medicinal Bath appears to be the most reliable complementary therapy. Acupuncture shows potential but requires further confirmation through more high-quality, large-scale randomized controlled trials.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261279443, identifier CRD420261279443.

records.title: Association of hyponatremia and risk of in-hospital mortality in patients with acute stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Association of hyponatremia and risk of in-hospital mortality in patients with acute stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Objective

Hyponatremia is among the most common electrolyte disturbances in acute stroke and has been increasingly recognized as a potential predictor of early complications. We aimed to evaluate whether hyponatremia on admission is associated with increased in-hospital mortality in patients with acute ischemic stroke (IS) and hemorrhagic stroke (HS).

Methods

We conducted a comprehensive systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Embase to identify relevant studies published between 1st January 2000 and 30th October 2025. Eligible studies included patients with acute stroke, reported admission serum sodium levels, and compared outcomes between hyponatremic and normonatremic groups. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using a random-effects model. Subgroup analyses were performed based on stroke type.

Results

Seventeen studies involving patients assessed within 24-72 h of stroke onset were included. Hyponatremia on admission was significantly associated with higher in-hospital mortality (RR 1.41, 95% CI 1.14-1.74). The association remained significant in ischemic stroke (RR 1.29, 95% CI 1.16-1.42) and in studies including mixed IS and HS populations (RR 1.59, 95% CI 1.19-2.12). No significant association was observed in hemorrhagic stroke alone (RR 1.47, 95% CI 0.70-3.10). Between-study heterogeneity was moderate (I 2 = 58.9%, p < 0.001). Funnel plot assessment suggested no significant publication bias.

Conclusions

Hyponatremia on admission is associated with increased in-hospital mortality in acute stroke, particularly in ischemic stroke. Early identification and management of hyponatremia may have prognostic and therapeutic relevance in acute stroke care.

Systematic review registration

PROSPERO: CRD420251110001.

records.title: The Current Landscape of Artificial Intelligence in Positron Emission Tomography (PET) Imaging Across the Cancer Continuum.

content.title: The Current Landscape of Artificial Intelligence in Positron Emission Tomography (PET) Imaging Across the Cancer Continuum.
content.abstract: PET scans have long been used in oncology imaging to provide molecular and metabolic information about diseases. The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in PET scans in oncology theranostics has the potential to optimise PET modality and overcome the constraints that PET scans have, such as semi-quantitative metrics, reader subjectivity, and variability across scanners/institutions. Advances in AI and radiomics are overcoming those limitations by deep learning lesion detection, enhancing image reconstruction, and improving noise resolution, which allows ultra-low dose acquisitions, while physics-informed models integrate with PET systems to strengthen interpretability and quantitative accuracy. There are also predictive AI frameworks that link PET imaging biomarkers to therapy response and outcomes, create individualised care and are even able to simulate treatment response and help with treatment planning. However, challenges do exist. Most AI PET studies are retrospective, single-centre, and underpowered (small sample), with limited external validation and inconsistent standardisation (in acquisition, segmentation, and extraction), leading to poor reproducibility and higher performance estimates. Furthermore, ethical considerations, including data protection and transparency, need to be considered before implementation. Federated learning, physics-informed frameworks, and adherence to standardised protocols offer steps towards regulated AI systems. In summary, PET is evolving from an imaging modality to a platform with the integration of deep learning, radiomics and reconstruction capable of predicting treatment response and guiding treatment. With rigorous prospective validation, cross-institutional collaboration, and regulatory standardisation, AI in PET would create an advancement in nuclear medicine imaging in oncology.

records.title: Comparative efficacy and safety of Chinese medicine external therapies for diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.

content.title: Comparative efficacy and safety of Chinese medicine external therapies for diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) is a chronic functional gastrointestinal disorder that significantly impairs patients' quality of life. While various Chinese medicine external therapies (CMETs) have been widely utilized, their relative superiority and safety remain poorly defined. This study aims to evaluate and rank the comparative efficacy and safety of different CMETs for IBS-D.

Methods

We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, The Cochrane Library, and CNKI from inception to March 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating CMETs for IBS-D. The primary outcomes were clinical total effective rate (TER) and the IBS Severity Scoring System (IBS-SSS). Secondary outcomes included IBS-Quality of Life (IBS-QOL), abdominal pain scores, and adverse events (AE). A frequentist network meta-analysis (NMA) was performed using the netmeta package in R software. Interventions were ranked using P-scores. Global and local inconsistency were assessed via Q-statistics and the node-splitting method.

Results

Twenty-two RCTs involving 11 distinct interventions were included. For the clinical total effective rate (TER), moxibustion (P-score = 0.8600) and tuina (P-score = 0.7130) emerged as the top-ranked interventions compared with Western medicine (WM) and placebo. Regarding symptom reduction (IBS-SSS) and abdominal pain relief, electroacupuncture (EA) (P-scores = 0.8854 and 0.8591, respectively) demonstrated superior efficacy over other modalities. Acupoint application combined with WM was found to be the most effective for improving quality of life (P-score = 1.0000). Safety analysis indicated that transcutaneous electrical acustimulation (TEA) (P-score = 0.8108) and placebo had the lowest risk of adverse events. Node-splitting analysis did not indicate statistically significant inconsistency; however, the findings should be interpreted cautiously because formal sensitivity analyses excluding high-risk studies were not feasible for all outcomes.

Conclusion

Chinese medicine external therapies may provide beneficial adjunctive or complementary options for patients with IBS-D. Moxibustion ranked highest for study-defined TER, whereas EA ranked highest for IBS-SSS and abdominal pain reduction. However, CINeMA assessment indicated low or very low confidence in several estimates; therefore, these rankings should be interpreted cautiously.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?RecordID=1324349, identifier CRD420261324349.

records.title: [Gynecology, Obstetrics and Fertility - Reborn in the Digital Revolution].

content.title: [Gynecology, Obstetrics and Fertility - Reborn in the Digital Revolution].
content.abstract:
Introduction

In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has brought about a dramatic transformation in obstetrics, gynecology, and fertility medicine. AI, including methods such as machine learning, deep learning, and large language models (LLMs), is reshaping the way clinical data are collected, analyzed, and applied. Image processing, particularly through deep learning applications, significantly enhances the detection of fetal anomalies in prenatal ultrasound, the classification of embryo quality in fertility treatments, and the early identification of gynecological pathologies. The integration of artificial intelligence systems with clinical expertise improves diagnostic accuracy, especially in the fields of medical imaging and pathology, while reducing the rate of false positive findings in imaging and pathology tests. However, artificial intelligence serves only as an assistive tool and does not replace medical judgment or established diagnostic standards. In parallel, machine learning models enable the prediction of pregnancy complications, the success of oncological treatments in gynecology and more. A major advantage of these models is their interpretability, which increases their potential for clinical adoption. LLMs contribute to the analysis of medical records, research summarization, and clinical decision support, although their use in other languages, such as Hebrew, remains limited. Augmented reality technologies offer new possibilities for enhancing patient experiences by reducing pain and anxiety during medical procedures. Despite the significant potential, challenges remain, including issues of data privacy and security, model reliability, and the need for appropriate regulatory frameworks. Israel, with its advanced yet heavily burdened healthcare system and high birth rates, is uniquely positioned to lead research and innovation in this field. Studying the capabilities and limitations of these tools will allow for their controlled and safe integration, promoting personalized medicine and optimizing public healthcare resource utilization. The aim of this study is to review advancements in implantation of AI tools in gynecology.

records.title: Leveraging artificial intelligence to predict non-adherence to pediatric immunization schedules: a systematic review.

content.title: Leveraging artificial intelligence to predict non-adherence to pediatric immunization schedules: a systematic review.
content.abstract:
Immunization is one of the most effective interventions to prevent infectious diseases. Identifying individuals at risk of non-adherence to immunization schedules could enable early interventions to improve coverage. With the increasing availability of large datasets with sociodemographic, medical, and geographic data, artificial intelligence (AI) offers new possibilities for identifying predictive patterns. We performed a systematic literature review of original studies that used AI to predict immunization non-adherence in children. Searches were conducted in PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science and no restrictions were applied regarding publication year, language, or study design. Study characteristics, dataset size, AI methods, performance metrics, and validation approaches were extracted. Risk of bias was assessed using PROBAST + AI. A total of 843 records were identified; after screening, 12 studies were included. Nine of 12 studies were conducted in low- and middle-income countries, used cross-sectional survey data, and analyzed vaccines from routine immunization schedules. Model performance was generally high; 9/12 studies reported an accuracy or an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve exceeding 80%, but no study conducted external validation. Predictors clustered into seven categories: maternal, paternal, family, child, geographic, wealth, and others. Among maternal and child-related factors, prenatal care and previous immunization history had a high predictive weight.

Conclusion

 AI demonstrates a promising potential for identifying individuals at risk of vaccine non-adherence. However, the lack of external validation raises concerns about model overfitting and limits real-world applicability. Demographic health surveys were routinely repeated across countries and time periods and could therefore represent an ideal resource for external validation.

What is known

• Geographic, sociodemographic, and medical factors contribute to non-adherence to the immunization schedule.   • Identifying these individuals can guide early interventions to improve immunization coverage.

What is new

• Artificial intelligence can reveal unknown influential factors; prenatal care and delivery setting emerged as key factors in this systematic review.

records.title: Exploring the efficacy of repeated low-level red-light therapy in retarding childhood myopia progression: updated systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Exploring the efficacy of repeated low-level red-light therapy in retarding childhood myopia progression: updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Due to the increasing prevalence of childhood myopia, low-level red-light therapy has surfaced as a non-pharmacological method to mitigate its advancement. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the efficacy of repeated low-level red-light (RLRL) in pediatric populations, providing evidence-based support for its therapeutic usage.

Methods

A search was performed in PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Embase, and prominent Chinese databases, including CNKI, VIP, and Wanfang, from their inception until May 13, 2025. This meta-analysis includes randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that matched the inclusion criteria and was analyzed using Stata software, version 18.0.

Results

This meta-analysis included 1,053 participants: 515 in the RLRL and 538 in the control groups. The SMD for SER reduction was 0.84 (95% CI: 0.50, 1.19), SMD for AL reduction was -1.01, (95% CI: -1.60, -0.41), and SMD for SFChT rise was 0.81 (95% CI: 0.65-0.98). There is no major publishing bias.

Conclusion

The meta-analysis found that children with myopia who got RLRL therapy in addition to normal treatment had significantly slower disease progression than the control group.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251034037, PROSPERO 2025 CRD420251034037.

records.title: Artificial intelligence and machine learning in diagnosing and managing temporomandibular disorders: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
records.publisher: Journal of oral biology and craniofacial research

content.title: Artificial intelligence and machine learning in diagnosing and managing temporomandibular disorders: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) models have recently emerged as promising tools for enhancing diagnostic accuracy.

Objective

To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of AI/ML models in detecting TMDs through a systematic review and meta-analysis of existing literature.

Methods

A comprehensive search of electronic databases was conducted to identify studies assessing the diagnostic performance of AI/ML models in TMD diagnosis (PROSPERO-CRD420251035080). Data extraction and quality assessment were conducted independently by two reviewers using the AXIS tool for cross-sectional and Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for cohort studies. Meta-analysis of diagnostic accuracy was performed using pooled sensitivity, specificity, diagnostic odds ratio, and area under the curve. Statistical heterogeneity was assessed with the I2 statistic.

Results

The systematic search identified 368 articles, of which 12 studies met inclusion criteria after screening. Risk of bias assessment showed most observational studies had low to unclear bias, while cross-sectional studies varied from moderate to high quality. Five studies were eligible for meta-analysis and they revealed that AI and machine learning models achieved a pooled sensitivity of 87.1 %(95 %CI:84.9 %-89.2 %) and specificity of 87.0 %(95 %CI:84.8 %-89.2 %) for TMD diagnosis. The diagnostic odds ratio was 45.1(95 %CI:30.5-66.8), with an area under the ROC curve of 0.96, indicating excellent diagnostic accuracy. Moderate heterogeneity I2 = 38.7 %.

Conclusion

AI/ML models demonstrate excellent accuracy in differentiating patients with and without TMDs, reinforcing their potential as reliable diagnostic aids in clinical and screening settings. However, variability in input features and lack of standardized model development protocols highlight the need for future research focusing on validation across diverse populations and harmonization of diagnostic criteria.

records.title: Natural Language Processing of Clinical Notes for Cancer Research and Patient Care Prior to Widespread Adoption of Generative AI: Scoping Review.

content.title: Natural Language Processing of Clinical Notes for Cancer Research and Patient Care Prior to Widespread Adoption of Generative AI: Scoping Review.
content.abstract:
Background

Clinical notes are the most abundant data type within electronic health records; however, their highly unstructured format presents significant challenges for supervised natural language processing (NLP) methods. The NLP community is increasingly adapting large language models to analyze clinical notes, achieving strong performance and generalizability with minimal task-specific fine-tuning. We conducted a scoping review of NLP methods applied to clinical notes prior to widespread adoption of generative artificial intelligence (AI) to establish a pre-large language model methodological baseline, showcase potential clinical utility, and highlight key challenges and limitations of extractive, supervised techniques that generative AI approaches may need to overcome.

Objective

This review aimed (1) to characterize the clinical notes used, (2) to identify NLP techniques used to analyze these notes, (3) to determine the clinical applications of NLP in cancer research and patient care, and (4) to highlight challenges and limitations of traditional pregenerative AI methods.

Methods

We systematically searched MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science for English-language studies published from January 1, 2014, to March 8, 2024. Retrieved references were imported into Covidence, a web-based platform that streamlines management of reviews. Two authors (ABK and HRAE) independently screened studies for eligibility and extracted data using a predefined data extraction template.

Results

A total of 226 studies were included in the review. Research using NLP to derive insights from clinical notes grew significantly, from 4 studies in 2014 to 43 in 2023. NLP methods have evolved from predominantly rule-based and ontology-driven approaches (2014-2017) to hybrid approaches that combine these with deep neural models such as Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (2018-2024). Most studies (161/226, 71.2%) developed their systems using small, single-institution datasets. Supervised learning approaches with manually annotated corpora were predominant (181/226, 80.1%). Most studies (174/226, 77%) focused on information extraction, with a few applying the extracted data to downstream tasks such as diagnostic and prognostic classification. Clinical domain pretrained models outperformed general domain pretrained models in the majority (11/16, 68.8%) of studies that evaluated multiple model types. In total, 25 studies compared their NLP-based systems with current practice in their respective clinical settings and reported potential benefits, including improved data coverage and completeness, faster information extraction, and improved classification or prediction accuracy. No studies evaluated the utility or impact of their systems in real-world clinical practice. The most common challenges reported by authors were restricted access to clinical notes (n=39) and limited data (n=18).

Conclusions

The application of NLP to clinical notes in oncology has expanded, but most studies focus on information extraction rather than downstream clinical tasks. Oncology NLP has the potential to advance cancer research and patient care, but barriers remain to robust evaluation and clinical deployment of promising tools. Emerging generative AI approaches will need to overcome these challenges to deliver real-world impact.

records.title: NK cell adoptive transfer in acute myeloid leukemia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: NK cell adoptive transfer in acute myeloid leukemia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) remains associated with high relapse rates and poor long-term survival, particularly in refractory patients or those ineligible for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). Adoptive transfer of natural killer (NK) cells has emerged as a promising immunotherapeutic strategy due to intrinsic cytotoxicity, low risk of graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), immune restoration capacity, and feasibility of allogeneic off-the-shelf manufacturing.

Methods

A systematic review of phase 1-2 clinical trials evaluating non-genetically modified NK-cell adoptive transfer was performed using PubMed and EMBASE (2000-2024). Study selection and data extraction were conducted independently by two reviewers in Rayyan®. Study characteristics, interventions, and outcomes were extracted. Response rate in relapsed/refractory (R/R) AML receiving NK monotherapy was pooled using single-proportion meta-analysis. One-year disease-free survival (DFS) in other settings was pooled by inverse variance using logarithm-transformed rates. Heterogeneity (I²), publication bias, and study quality (NIH before-after tool) were assessed.

Results

Of 790 records identified, 29 studies were included, predominantly single-arm phase I/II trials (one randomized phase II). In R/R AML (11 studies; 217 patients), pooled response rate was 35% (95% CI 29-42; I²=30%), with 20.2% proceeding to HSCT. Higher responses were observed in strategies enhancing NK activation or persistence, including expanded multi-infusion platforms and CIML-NK. In low-/intermediate-risk AML in remission (3 studies; 38 patients), pooled 1-year DFS was 82% (95% CI 56-100; I²=0). In high-risk AML in remission and ineligible for HSCT (5 studies; 59 patients), pooled 1-year DFS was 26% (95% CI 12-55; I²=84). In studies combining NK transfer with haploidentical HSCT (9 studies; 303 patients), pooled 1-year DFS was 40% (95% CI 27-57; I²=94). Toxicities were generally mild, GVHD rates were low (0-8%), and severe events were uncommon. NK-cell persistence was typically short, improving with multiple infusions and CIML approaches.

Conclusion

Adoptive allogeneic NK-cell transfer appears safe and clinically promising, particularly for patients unfit for intensive therapy or HSCT. At present, its use should remain limited to clinical trials. Future studies should define the optimal approach that maximizes clinical activity while maintaining low toxicity and achieving durable persistence of allogeneic NK cells.

records.title: Endovenous laser ablation versus radiofrequency ablation in chronic venous insufficiency: a comparative meta-analysis of efficacy and safety.

content.title: Endovenous laser ablation versus radiofrequency ablation in chronic venous insufficiency: a comparative meta-analysis of efficacy and safety.
content.abstract:
Background

Chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) is a common vascular disorder that substantially impairs quality of life. Endovenous laser ablation (EVLA) and radiofrequency ablation (RFA) have largely replaced conventional surgery; however, their comparative efficacy and safety-particularly across follow-up time points and EVLA wavelengths-remain debated.

Methods

We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar from inception to September 2024. Thirty-three comparative studies (9 randomized controlled trials and 24 non-randomized studies) involving 22,814 patients (8,144 EVLA and 14,670 RFA) were included. Analyses were performed at the patient level. The single primary outcome was complete occlusion of the treated vein; all other endpoints were secondary. Secondary outcomes included procedural success, recanalization, partial occlusion, reflux-free rate, postoperative pain, recurrence, return to work or daily activities, patient satisfaction, and complications, with stratified analyses by follow-up time and EVLA wavelength.

Results

RFA was associated with significantly lower postoperative pain at 6 weeks (mean difference [MD] = -3.00; 95% CI: -3.42 to -2.58) and 6 months (MD = -1.00; 95% CI: -1.85 to -0.14), and a reduced risk of paresthesia at 1 month (odds ratio [OR] = 0.52; 95% CI: 0.28-0.95). Non-randomized studies suggested lower recurrence rates with RFA compared with EVLA (OR = 0.42; 95% CI: 0.29-0.62), although randomized trials showed no significant difference. Complete occlusion rates were lower with RFA than with EVLA in pooled analyses (OR = 0.07; 95% CI: 0.04-0.14), particularly at early follow-up (1 day: OR = 0.01; 95% CI: 0.00-0.11), with differences diminishing over time. Variation in outcome definitions and imaging timing likely contributed to these early effects. Reflux-free rates and patient-reported outcomes, including Aberdeen Varicose Vein Questionnaire scores, did not differ significantly between groups.

Conclusion

Both EVLA and RFA are effective and safe treatments for CVI. RFA provides advantages in short-term postoperative comfort and selected complications, whereas EVLA-particularly with 1,470-nm wavelengths-achieves more consistent early technical occlusion. However, these differences do not translate into clear differences in reflux-free status or patient-reported quality-of-life outcomes, supporting individualized treatment selection. When performed competently, neither modality offers a clinically meaningful advantage for patient-centered outcomes.

records.title: The Use of Artificial Intelligence in Planning Dental Implant Procedures: A Systematic Review.

content.title: The Use of Artificial Intelligence in Planning Dental Implant Procedures: A Systematic Review.
content.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being integrated into dental implantology, particularly in treatment planning, a critical phase for implant success. Traditionally dependent on clinician expertise, planning can now be supported by AI-assisted systems that aim to improve diagnostic accuracy, precision, and efficiency. Objective: To synthesise recent evidence on the use of AI in dental implant planning, particularly its ability to analyse cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) imaging to identify edentulous regions and assess bone dimensions compared with conventional planning methods. Methods: A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, and the Cochrane Library, with additional manual searches from October 2024 to July 2025. Eligibility was defined using the Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome (PICO) framework, focusing on adults undergoing implant procedures planned using AI-assisted CBCT imaging and deep learning (DL) models, particularly U-Net architectures, for CBCT segmentation. Results: Ten studies were included, AI systems demonstrated high accuracy (92-99.7%) in detecting teeth and edentulous regions, with precision and recall frequently exceeding 90%. AI-assisted planning also showed improved efficiency, and, in one study, higher implant success rates compared with traditional planning (92% vs. 78%). However, variability in study design, inconsistent reporting, and limited ethical oversight were noted. Conclusions: AI, particularly DL models applied to CBCT imaging, shows strong potential to enhance diagnostic precision and efficiency in dental implant planning. Nevertheless, the field requires standardised evaluation metrics, larger datasets, and well-designed clinical trials before widespread clinical implementation.

records.title: Efficacy and safety of fecal microbiota transplantation for chronic constipation: a systematic review and meta-analysis integrating pre-post and single-arm evidence.

content.title: Efficacy and safety of fecal microbiota transplantation for chronic constipation: a systematic review and meta-analysis integrating pre-post and single-arm evidence.
content.abstract:
Background

Chronic constipation is a common functional gastrointestinal disorder with a global prevalence of 12%-17%. Conventional treatments have limited efficacy for refractory cases, with high recurrence and side effects. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) offers a novel strategy by restoring gut microecological balance, yet its efficacy requires systematic evaluation. This meta-analysis evaluated FMT efficacy and safety through an innovative "three-in-one" framework.

Methods

We systematically searched CENTRAL, PubMed, Embase, and CNKI for RCTs, single-arm studies, and cohort studies. The framework comprised: (1) RCT random-effects meta-analysis; (2) single-arm proportional meta-analysis with Freeman-Tukey transformation; (3) pre-post paired sensitivity analysis (r = 0.5, with sensitivity tests at r = 0.3, 0.7, 0.9). Publication bias was assessed via Egger, Harbord, trim-and-fill, and fail-safe N tests.

Results

12 RCTs (n = 1040), 16 single-arm studies (n = 403), and 4 cohort studies (n = 422) were included. After trim-and-fill adjustment for publication bias, FMT was associated with a clinical total response rate of RR = 1.21 (95% CI: 1.10-1.33). The unadjusted pooled estimate was RR = 1.36 (95% CI: 1.21-1.52, P < 0.001); however, the Harbord test indicated potential publication bias (P = 0.003), necessitating this correction. Wexner score improved (MD = -2.08, 95% CI: -3.35 to -0.81, P = 0.003). Among the 16 single-arm studies, 8 (n = 249) reported remission/improvement rates, showing a remission rate of 51.7% (95% CI: 40.3%-62.9%) and paired pre-post improvements in BSFS, Wexner, and PAC-QOL; these within-group changes cannot establish causal efficacy. During follow-up periods of up to 24 weeks, no serious adverse events were reported; long-term safety data are lacking.

Conclusion

Current evidence suggests FMT is a promising therapeutic option for chronic constipation, with an adjusted clinical total response rate of RR = 1.21 (95% CI: 1.10-1.33) after correction for publication bias. While FMT was associated with improvements in symptom scores, quality of life, and intestinal function, the evidence quality is limited by publication bias, high heterogeneity, and high risk of bias in all included RCTs. More high-quality, sham-controlled RCTs are needed to validate these findings.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?ID=CRD420261394673, identifier: CRD420261394673.

records.title: Identification of metabolic vulnerabilities and synthetic lethal targets utilizing artificial intelligence-driven precision medicine.

content.title: Identification of metabolic vulnerabilities and synthetic lethal targets utilizing artificial intelligence-driven precision medicine.
content.abstract: Cancer metabolism is highly plastic, and most attempts to turn that plasticity into a therapeutic target fail for a specific, recurring reason: a computational prediction of a metabolic vulnerability is not the same evidentiary object as an experimentally confirmed one, and the two are routinely discussed as if they were interchangeable. This review takes that distinction as its starting point rather than its conclusion. Artificial intelligence and genome-scale systems biology have made it easy to generate metabolic hypotheses at a scale no experimental program could match - machine learning models trained on genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data now output candidate vulnerabilities, biomarkers, and drug combinations faster than they can be tested - but the resulting literature has not been consistently honest about how far any given prediction has actually traveled toward clinical relevance. We examine six areas where this gap is most visible: multi-omics data integration, genome-scale metabolic network modeling, computational discovery of metabolic vulnerabilities and synthetic lethal interactions, single-cell and spatial resolution of metabolic heterogeneity, AI-guided drug and biomarker discovery, and the small set of studies that have actually reached clinical testing. Rather than summarizing these areas as separate literatures, we grade every substantive finding discussed against an explicit four-tier evidence standard - associative, mechanistic, perturbation-validated, or clinically tested - and we apply that standard critically rather than deferentially: several widely cited computational vulnerabilities remain unconfirmed outside the cell lines in which they were discovered, genome-scale models continue to carry unresolved gaps in reaction coverage that limit their predictive reach, and, of the AI-derived metabolic predictions discussed in this review, only one has so far been tested in a completed prospective clinical trial. We argue that this shortage of prospective validation, not a shortage of computational sophistication, is the field's central constraint, and we close by identifying where methodological effort would do the most good: standardized validation reporting, tissue-resolved rather than bulk metabolic models, and closer coupling between computational prediction and the specific experimental designs capable of falsifying it.

records.title: Operationalising digital and AI pathology in translational research and drug development: an infrastructure and regulatory perspective from biobank to companion diagnostic.

content.title: Operationalising digital and AI pathology in translational research and drug development: an infrastructure and regulatory perspective from biobank to companion diagnostic.
content.abstract: Digital and artificial intelligence (AI) pathology have advanced rapidly and are increasingly embedded in translational research, clinical trials and regulated diagnostic devices. Multiple reviews have addressed the underlying computational methods, oncology applications and clinical translation barriers; however, the operational and regulatory infrastructure required to deploy these technologies across the full drug-development pipeline remains under-reviewed. This structured narrative review synthesises peer-reviewed literature and regulatory documents identified through searches of PubMed, Embase and Web of Science between January 2019 and April 2026 (78 sources retained) on the end-to-end ecosystem connecting AI-ready tissue biobanks, preclinical pathology, AI-assisted patient screening, clinical-trial endpoint adjudication, central pathology review, Contract Research Organization (CRO) workflows and US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulatory pathways governing In Vitro Diagnostics (IVD), Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) and Companion Diagnostics (CDx). Unlike prior method-centric or oncology-clinician-centric reviews, we focus on the infrastructure between models and patients, including Laboratory Information Systems (LIS), Image Management Systems (IMS), AI orchestration and structured reporting under Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments, College of American Pathologists, Good Laboratory Practice, Good Clinical Laboratory Practice, Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act and FDA frameworks. We provide a vendor-agnostic comparison of integrated pathology platforms, a mapping of FDA regulatory pathways (510(k), De Novo, premarket approval) to digital-pathology product categories, a stage-by-stage map from each drug-development challenge to its enabling infrastructure and regulatory framework, and a critical appraisal of the unresolved bottlenecks that gate broad adoption: domain shift, interpretability, annotation cost, algorithmic bias, external validation, regulatory uncertainty and reimbursement. A governed, interoperable LIS, IMS and AI ecosystem is a prerequisite for translating digital-pathology research into regulator-grade evidence. Priorities include external validation against reporting standards (Transparent Reporting of a multivariable prediction model for Individual Prognosis or Diagnosis - Artificial Intelligence (TRIPOD-AI), Checklist for Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging (CLAIM), Development and Early-stage Clinical Identification and Delegation Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence (DECIDE-AI)), harmonisation with the EU AI Act and EU Medical Device Regulation and cost-effectiveness evaluation in real-world deployment.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in emergency trauma perioperative management: applications, performance benchmarks, and translation barriers.

content.title: Artificial intelligence in emergency trauma perioperative management: applications, performance benchmarks, and translation barriers.
content.abstract: This review examines the current status of artificial intelligence (AI) applications in the perioperative management of emergency trauma. Published studies suggest performance advantages of AI over traditional methods in prehospital triage, radiographic injury detection, massive transfusion prediction, and early warning of postoperative complications, although findings vary across study designs and validation settings. However, actual adoption in trauma care remains limited due to data heterogeneity, performance degradation in external validation, workflow integration challenges, lack of interpretability, and a scarcity of prospective interventional evidence. This review further argues that methodologically inflated benchmark performance constitutes an underrecognized barrier to adoption in its own right, and that bridging the implementation gap will likely require a shift from area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC)-centered reporting toward reporting sensitivity at prespecified clinical thresholds and evaluating patient outcomes in prospective interventional trials.

records.title: A Case-Based Framework for Teaching Artificial Intelligence Applications in Medical Education.
records.publisher: MedEdPORTAL : the journal of teaching and learning resources

content.title: A Case-Based Framework for Teaching Artificial Intelligence Applications in Medical Education.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML)-based tools are emerging across many areas of medicine. The next generation of medical professionals must be prepared to critically assess the tools they will use, including how they work and the ethical or legal implications of their implementation. To address this need, we developed a generalizable case-writing framework that enables educators and learners to engage with clinical cases integrating AI/ML concepts, clinical reasoning, and ethical considerations.

Methods

We designed a case-writing template to compose clinical case scenarios that integrate clinical, technical, and ethical/legal learning objectives relating to AI applications in medicine. Medical students used this template to construct 3 cases. Student-authored cases were presented to a broader audience in 1-hour sessions: first as a pilot event, then as a class-wide lecture for 140 fourth-year medical students in a transition-into-residency course.

Results

After the sessions, student audiences had a statistically significant increase in familiarity with key AI terminology, a greater appreciation for the importance of ethical considerations of AI applications in health care, and an increased perceived importance of integrating AI-related topics into the medical curriculum.

Discussion

A case-based framework provides a scalable approach to integrating AI education into existing curricula by connecting clinical scenarios with technical concepts and the ethical considerations of AI adoption; cases offer a familiar format that helps learners understand AI applications in patient care while exploring implementation challenges. The case-writing template and 3 sample cases are provided as adaptable resources for educators seeking to incorporate AI literacy.

records.title: Integrating predictive modeling, imaging, and EHR-linked decision support in spine informatics.
records.publisher: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society

content.title: Integrating predictive modeling, imaging, and EHR-linked decision support in spine informatics.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming spine care by enabling analysis of imaging, clinical, and textual data to support diagnosis, risk stratification, and treatment planning. Techniques including deep learning-based image analysis, radiomics, and natural language processing (NLP) offer opportunities to standardize interpretation and derive quantitative biomarkers beyond human visual assessment. This narrative review examines recent innovations in spine-focused biomedical informatics and evaluates their clinical relevance and translational challenges.

Methods

A narrative review was conducted, focusing on AI in spine care across imaging, radiomics, NLP of electronic health records, and clinical decision support. Literature was selected via targeted PubMed searches; studies describing technical development, validation, and clinical implementation were synthesized, addressing explainability, uncertainty, workflow, and regulation.

Results

Convolutional neural networks enable vertebral and disc segmentation, detection of degenerative and traumatic pathology, and quantitative assessment of paraspinal musculature. Radiomics approaches extract high-dimensional imaging features that improve the prediction of osteoporosis, fracture risk, tumor characterization, and surgical outcomes. NLP techniques, including emerging large language models, unlock clinically relevant information from unstructured text, enhancing outcome prediction and population-level analyses. Multimodal clinical decision support systems integrating imaging, EHR data, and NLP-derived features demonstrate promise for personalized risk assessment and treatment guidance. Challenges remain regarding data heterogeneity, generalizability, privacy, and prospective validation.

Conclusion

AI-driven biomedical informatics holds substantial promise to enhance diagnostic accuracy, prognostication, and personalized decision-making in spine care. Successful clinical translation will require robust validation, explainable, uncertainty-aware models, regulatory alignment, and integration into clinical workflows to ensure safe, trustworthy, and patient-centered adoption.

records.title: Personas shift clinical action thresholds in large language models.

content.title: Personas shift clinical action thresholds in large language models.
content.abstract: Clinical large language model (LLM) deployment is shifting from feasibility to liability, while current guidance largely treats model behavior as a control problem. We tested whether decision-style system prompts shift clinical action thresholds when clinical facts are held constant, and whether these shifts are consistent across settings and models. We defined nine physician personas by crossing three ethical orientations (duty-based, care-based, utilitarian) with three cognitive styles (intuitive, integrative, analytic). Twenty open-weight LLMs were evaluated on 2500 simulated emergency department vignettes and 2500 MIMIC-IV-Note discharge summaries. For each text, models answered five binary decision items (safety, autonomy, treatment, resource use, follow-up). Each condition was repeated ten times, yielding 5,000,000 total decisions. Under baseline prompting, models answered "Yes" to 42.8% of decisions. Persona prompts shifted affirmative rates from 36.9% to 46.4%, a 9.5 percentage-point swing under fixed clinical evidence. Effects were largest in autonomy and treatment and were consistent across corpora (85.7% directional agreement; r = 0.82 for effect sizes). Susceptibility varied by model (4.9-16.1 points), with no consistent protection from medical fine-tuning or model size. Decision-style system prompts reliably change clinical action thresholds in LLMs under fixed evidence. Prompting is a policy-setting layer, not just a communication layer, and should be treated as a first-class deployment configuration.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Coronary Artery Disease: From Detection to Precision Management.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Coronary Artery Disease: From Detection to Precision Management.
content.abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide, yet the landscape is rapidly evolving as artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to its detection, diagnosis, and management. This review surveys the expanding role of AI across the full spectrum of CAD care. In screening, deep-learning electrocardiography and electronic health record-based digital markers enable earlier identification of clinically significant disease. In noninvasive imaging, AI-driven coronary computed tomography angiography automates calcium scoring, derives fractional flow reserve without invasive wires, and quantifies high-risk plaque features that predict incident adverse events. Within the cardiac catheterization laboratory, angiography-derived physiologic assessment and AI-guided intravascular imaging segmentation support real-time procedural decision-making. Beyond diagnosis, machine-learning models integrating multimodality imaging data improve risk stratification over conventional clinical scores, while pharmacogenomic algorithms and wearable-based digital rehabilitation platforms enable patient-centric secondary prevention. Despite this progress, significant challenges persist, including limited evidence from randomized trials, algorithmic bias in underrepresented populations, regulatory uncertainty surrounding software-as-a-medical-device frameworks, and the risk of clinician de-skilling. AI has the potential to act as a collaborative tool that augments-rather than replaces-physician judgment. Future directions include foundation models, multiomics integration, agentic AI workflows, and equity-centered deployment strategies to ensure that AI-driven advances benefit all individuals with CAD.

records.title: Emerging Computational Advances in Simulating PCSK9 Variant Dynamics for Therapeutic Design Against Hypercholesterolemia.

content.title: Emerging Computational Advances in Simulating PCSK9 Variant Dynamics for Therapeutic Design Against Hypercholesterolemia.
content.abstract: Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) is a premier model for precision medicine, having moved from genetic discovery to approved therapeutics within two decades. Yet despite the clinical success of monoclonal antibodies, small interfering RNA and the newly approved oral macrocyclic-peptide inhibitor class, targeting PCSK9 remains a demanding biophysical challenge. Clinical translation has concentrated almost entirely on the rigid, well-resolved subtilisin-like catalytic domain that interfaces with the low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR). By contrast, the C-terminal cysteine- and histidine-rich domain (CHRD), which governs allosteric regulation, protein trafficking and post-translational modification, is highly disordered and largely elusive in experimental structures, leaving a critical regulatory network therapeutically unexploited. This review examines how advanced computational biology is bridging that structural gap, organizing the computational landscape of PCSK9 around the biophysical mechanisms of gain- and loss-of-function variants. We detail how explicit-solvent molecular dynamics, free-energy calculations and cryptic-pocket detection expose the functional plasticity and allosteric networks that static crystallography cannot capture, and we evaluate the convergence of these physics-based approaches with artificial intelligence, including deep-learning structure prediction and generative design of de novo nanobody and peptide binders. Therapeutic development and the structural literature currently point in diverging directions: drug discovery remains focused on the crowded LDLR-binding interface, whereas computational methods are beginning to identify candidate sites beyond it. We argue that the next advance in PCSK9 therapeutics will come from integrating generative artificial intelligence with rigorous enhanced sampling in a unified pipeline, deliberately shifting focus toward the disordered regulatory domains that have evaded classical screening.

records.title: Beyond Accuracy: Validation, Reproducibility, and Deployment Readiness of AI in Food Safety and Quality.

content.title: Beyond Accuracy: Validation, Reproducibility, and Deployment Readiness of AI in Food Safety and Quality.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly proposed for detecting microbial and chemical hazards in food, but laboratory accuracies are rarely reproduced in routine use. This structured narrative review examined whether reported performance is traceable, independently validated, and transferable to operational settings. Eight bibliographic databases and seven institutional routes were searched for English-language records published from January 2018 to May 2026, and we screened the records; the final corpus comprised 76 sources (53 journal articles, 9 conference papers, 2 preprints, and 12 institutional or regulatory documents). Seven primary studies supporting the quantitative evidence were appraised individually against 11 indicators, including test-set independence, external validation, and leakage control. Physical-hazard inspection and narrow-matrix spectral grading had the strongest deployment evidence, whereas microbial and chemical screening remained at laboratory or pilot scale. Among the appraised studies, the most credible estimates came from physically or temporally independent test sets, and no sensor-based study evaluated transfer to another instrument or laboratory. Deep learning showed clear advantages for image-based tasks but not consistently for small-sample spectral calibration. Adoption is limited mainly by validation design, recalibration burden, false-alarm costs, and the absence of a regulatory pathway rather than by accuracy. AI is best positioned as a screening and decision-support layer linked to confirmatory testing and human oversight.

records.title: AI-Enabled Animal Behavior Analysis for Translational Pharmacology and Therapeutic Discovery.

content.title: AI-Enabled Animal Behavior Analysis for Translational Pharmacology and Therapeutic Discovery.
content.abstract: Animal behavior is a critical endpoint in preclinical pharmacology, toxicology, and therapeutic discovery, yet conventional behavioral scoring remains labor-intensive, low-dimensional, and difficult to reproduce across laboratories. Artificial intelligence (AI) can now quantify behavior from video with greater spatial, temporal, and phenotypic resolution. This review summarizes how object detection, markerless pose estimation, unsupervised behavioral segmentation, foundation models, and autonomous analysis agents are reshaping behavioral phenotyping. General-purpose object detectors rapidly localize and track animals, whereas open-source pose-estimation tools extend measurement beyond centroid tracking to body-part trajectories and fine motor patterns; paired with supervised classifiers, they have matched human scoring and exceeded some commercial systems. Technical accuracy alone does not establish behavioral construct validity or pharmacological validity. Unsupervised methods such as Motion Sequencing represent drug responses and disease-model phenotypes as structured changes in behavioral states rather than only as predefined endpoints, providing high-dimensional fingerprints of pharmacological action. Segmentation and tracking foundation models may reduce annotation burden but require validation across species, strain, sex, apparatus, and paradigm. AI agents may assist with literature review, code generation, analysis auditing, and figure production but must remain within transparent, human-supervised workflows. In behavioral pharmacology, pose estimation is established as a measurement method and emerging as a drug-effect endpoint, supervised classification and unsupervised segmentation are emerging, and foundation models and agents remain prospective. AI-enabled behavioral analysis can become a reproducible phenotyping layer for drug discovery and toxicology if researchers adopt open pipelines, rigorous validation, and reporting standards, rather than replacing one opaque measurement system with another.

records.title: Artificial intelligence for precision nephrology: current evidence to clinical translation and future prospects.

content.title: Artificial intelligence for precision nephrology: current evidence to clinical translation and future prospects.
content.abstract:
Background and objectives

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied across nephrology, with potential applications spanning disease prediction, diagnosis, treatment optimisation, and clinical decision support. However, reported model performance varies substantially across clinical domains, and high predictive performance does not necessarily demonstrate clinical utility or readiness for deployment. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the applications of AI in nephrology and critically evaluates the methodological maturity, validation, interpretability, fairness, and translational readiness of AI systems across major nephrology domains.

Methods

A structured literature search of PubMed was conducted using terms related to AI and nephrology, with the primary eligibility period restricted to studies published from 2020 to 2025. The search strategy incorporated artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning, neural networks, natural language processing, large language models, generative AI, computer vision, reinforcement learning, federated learning, and related terms, together with nephrology and kidney-disease terms. Title/abstract and full-text screening were performed independently by the first and second authors, with disagreements resolved by the third author. Two foundational pre-2020 studies identified through citation chaining were retained because of their importance to the subsequent development of AI applications in nephrology. Evidence was synthesized qualitatively according to study design, validation, predictive performance, interpretability, fairness, prospective evaluation, and translational readiness.

Results

AI applications were identified across acute kidney injury, chronic kidney disease, nephropathology, kidney transplantation, haemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis, large language models, reinforcement learning, and federated learning. Across these domains, many models demonstrated promising discrimination, but evidence maturity varied considerably. External validation was present for some applications, whereas prospective evaluation and evidence of clinical utility remained limited. The literature also highlighted challenges related to calibration, generalizability, interpretability, algorithmic fairness, data governance, and integration into clinical workflows. Large language models and federated learning represent emerging areas, but nephrology-specific evidence remains comparatively limited.

Conclusions

AI has substantial potential to support precision nephrology, but technical performance should not be equated with clinical effectiveness or deployment readiness. Future research should prioritize external and prospective validation, assessment of clinical utility and patient outcomes, transparent reporting, fairness, regulatory oversight, and effective human-AI integration.

records.title: Augmentation or erosion? Artificial intelligence and the transformation of clinical reasoning: a critical narrative review.

content.title: Augmentation or erosion? Artificial intelligence and the transformation of clinical reasoning: a critical narrative review.
content.abstract:
Background

Artificial intelligence (AI) systems are used to support diagnosis, but a model's accuracy does not establish that clinicians reason more accurately when they use it. This review appraises how AI decision support and large language models affect physicians' diagnostic performance and the risks of relying on them.

Methods

This critical narrative review follows the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles. Scopus, PubMed/MEDLINE, SciELO and LILACS were searched in July and August 2026 in English, Spanish and Portuguese. Eligible studies, published from 2015 onward, compared AI-assisted with unassisted clinicians, measured reliance on AI or unassisted performance after exposure to it, or externally validated deployed models. A single author selected sources purposively. Nine primary studies were appraised with an adapted Critical Appraisal Skills Programme framework.

Results

In randomized trials of perceptual tasks, AI support improved detection. In the MASAI mammography screening trial, cancer detection rose from 5.0 to 6.4 per 1,000 women, reading workload fell by 44%, and the interval-cancer rate was non-inferior. In colonoscopy, computer-aided detection raised the adenoma detection rate from 40.4% to 54.8%. In the only randomized trial of open-ended diagnostic reasoning, access to GPT-4 did not improve physicians' scores (76% vs. 74%; P=.60 ), although the model alone scored 92%. Evidence of harm came from smaller or non-randomized studies: reader accuracy fell sharply when AI suggestions were incorrect or the AI missed a cancer; physicians trained in AI literacy were still misled by erroneous model advice; unassisted adenoma detection fell from 28.4% to 22.4% after routine AI use in one pre-post study; and a deployed sepsis model discriminated poorly on external validation (area under the curve 0.63). No eligible study from Latin America was identified.

Conclusions

In the studies reviewed, AI assistance improved clinician performance in bounded detection tasks but not in open-ended diagnostic reasoning, where evidence is limited to one vignette-based trial. The evidence that reliance on AI can impair performance comes from single or design-limited studies and does not establish how large or lasting such effects are. Benefit therefore cannot be inferred from model accuracy alone; assisted and unassisted clinician performance should be measured directly.

records.title: Artificial intelligence-based voice biomarkers for early detection and monitoring of neurological diseases: current evidence, limitations, and clinical perspectives.

content.title: Artificial intelligence-based voice biomarkers for early detection and monitoring of neurological diseases: current evidence, limitations, and clinical perspectives.
content.abstract:
Background

Early diagnosis and longitudinal monitoring of neurological diseases remain major clinical challenges because current diagnostic approaches are often expensive, invasive, or insufficiently sensitive to detect early functional changes. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising approach for analyzing voice and speech as non-invasive digital biomarkers capable of capturing subtle alterations associated with neurological dysfunction.

Methods

This narrative review analyzed studies published between 2015 and 2026 retrieved from PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar. The review critically examines the limitations of current neurological diagnostic methods, summarizes the available evidence on AI-based voice and speech biomarkers, discusses machine learning and deep learning approaches applied to speech analysis, and evaluates the methodological, ethical, and regulatory challenges that currently limit their clinical implementation.

Results

Current evidence indicates that AI-based voice biomarkers have considerable potential for screening, diagnostic support, and longitudinal monitoring of neurological disorders, including Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease, multiple sclerosis, and other neurodegenerative conditions. Several studies report high diagnostic performance under controlled experimental settings. However, substantial heterogeneity in study design, sample size, languages, speech acquisition protocols, validation strategies, and reporting standards limits direct comparison between studies and hinders clinical translation. External validation and prospective multicenter studies remain scarce.

Conclusion

AI-based voice analysis represents a promising, scalable, and non-invasive complement to conventional neurological assessment, with particular potential for remote screening and disease monitoring. Nevertheless, current evidence does not yet support routine clinical implementation. Future progress will depend on standardized speech acquisition protocols, robust external validation across diverse populations, explainable AI models, and regulatory frameworks capable of ensuring safety, reproducibility, and clinical reliability.

records.title: Clinical integration of artificial intelligence for diagnosis, risk prediction and management of rare cardiovascular diseases.
records.publisher: Journal of basic and clinical physiology and pharmacology

content.title: Clinical integration of artificial intelligence for diagnosis, risk prediction and management of rare cardiovascular diseases.
content.abstract:
Introduction

RCDs comprise a diverse group of inherited and acquired disorders characterized by low prevalence, substantial genetic and phenotypic heterogeneity, delayed diagnosis, and limited evidence-based therapeutic options. These challenges contribute to poor clinical outcomes, including progressive heart failure, malignant arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death.

Content

This review summarizes recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) for the diagnosis and management of RCDs. AI technologies, including machine learning, deep learning, and multimodal data integration, enable comprehensive analysis of electrocardiography, echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, computed tomography, genomic and multi-omics data, biomarkers, wearable devices, and electronic health records. These approaches improve early disease detection, phenotypic classification, risk stratification, prognostic prediction and personalized treatment planning.

Summary

Current evidence suggests that AI significantly enhances diagnostic accuracy, prognostic assessment, and individualized clinical decision-making in patients with RCDs.

Outlook

Future clinical implementation requires standardized multicenter datasets, prospective validation, transparent and explainable algorithms, robust regulatory and ethical frameworks, and seamless integration into healthcare systems. Continued interdisciplinary collaboration will accelerate AI-driven precision cardiovascular medicine and improve outcomes for patients with rare cardiovascular diseases.

records.title: Growth, Specialty Distribution, and Regulatory Pathways of Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Medical Devices Authorized in the United States From 1995 to 2026: A Cross-Sectional Analysis.

content.title: Growth, Specialty Distribution, and Regulatory Pathways of Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Medical Devices Authorized in the United States From 1995 to 2026: A Cross-Sectional Analysis.
content.abstract: Introduction The United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) publishes a list of artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled medical devices authorized for marketing. Annual authorizations have risen sharply in recent years, and an updated analysis of the complete list is needed. This study aimed to characterize regulatory authorizations on the full list through mid-2026. Methods A cross-sectional analysis of all 1,614 entries on the FDA AI-Enabled Medical Device List (final decisions from September 1995 to June 2026) was performed. Regulatory pathway, year, lead review panel, product code, and manufacturer group were derived for each entry. Growth was estimated by log-linear regression, trends were tested with the Cochran-Armitage test and logistic regression with manufacturer-clustered standard errors, and associations were tested with chi-squared and Fisher exact tests, with Holm adjustment for multiple testing. Results Annual authorizations rose from 18 in 2016 to 335 in 2025, an estimated growth of 35.3% per year (95% confidence interval (CI) 27.0-44.3), and 977 of 1,614 entries (60.5%) were authorized from 2023 onward. Radiology accounted for 1,230 entries (76.2%); its share peaked at 347 of 405 (85.7%) in 2020-2022 and fell to 750 of 977 (76.8%) in 2023-2026 (p < 0.001), while radiology authorizations kept growing in absolute terms and the number of represented specialty panels rose from 10 to 16. The 510(k) pathway accounted for 1,553 authorizations (96.2%), and radiology entries were less likely than others to use the De Novo or premarket approval pathways (18 of 1,230, 1.5% vs. 43 of 384, 11.2%; odds ratio 0.14, 95% CI 0.08-0.27 after adjustment for era). Of 40 De Novo grants, 22 created product codes that later received 181 510(k) clearances. Imaging systems such as ultrasound, computed tomography, and magnetic resonance scanners accounted for 399 entries (24.7%), and seven large manufacturers accounted for 288 of these (72.2%). Findings were similar for 1,195 deduplicated devices and for entries through December 2025. Conclusions FDA authorization of AI-enabled devices continues to accelerate. Radiology remains dominant and still growing, while other specialties are expanding alongside it; the 510(k) pathway predominates, and a growing share of authorizations concerns AI embedded in imaging equipment. These findings describe regulatory authorizations rather than clinical adoption, and they identify transparency about AI functions in conventional devices and AI-specific post-market surveillance as topics for further study.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in the diagnosis of necrotising enterocolitis from abdominal radiographs: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Artificial intelligence in the diagnosis of necrotising enterocolitis from abdominal radiographs: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Context

Necrotising enterocolitis (NEC) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in premature and very low birth weight neonates. Early diagnosis is challenging as clinical and laboratory features are non-specific. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers a potential means to improve diagnostic consistency and timeliness.

Objective

To systematically review and meta-analyse the diagnostic accuracy of AI-based models for identifying NEC from abdominal radiographs.

Evidence acquisition

A systematic search of MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, IEEE Xplore, and the Cochrane Library was conducted for studies published between January 1, 2015, and July 20, 2025. Studies evaluating AI, machine learning, or deep learning models applied to abdominal radiographs for NEC diagnosis or stratification, and reporting diagnostic performance metrics, were included. Study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment (modified PROBAST) were performed independently by two reviewers. Diagnostic accuracy was pooled using hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic models.

Results

Ten retrospective studies met inclusion criteria; six were eligible for meta-analysis. Most employed convolutional neural networks, with limited external validation. The pooled sensitivity for AI-based diagnosis of NEC was 0.78 (95% CI 0.67-0.85) and pooled specificity was 0.84 (95% CI 0.73-0.91), with substantial heterogeneity. Positive and negative likelihood ratios were 4.84 and 0.27, respectively, indicating moderate diagnostic value. Explainability analyses commonly highlighted clinically relevant bowel features.

Conclusion

AI-based interpretation of abdominal radiographs demonstrates moderate accuracy for NEC diagnosis and may serve as a decision-support adjunct rather than a standalone test. Clinicians should view these tools as complementary aids within existing diagnostic frameworks, pending prospective validation of AI models and standardised implementation into existing workflows.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251090229.

records.title: Current status, evidence maturity, and translational readiness of artificial intelligence in dentistry: a bibliometric and thematic analysis.

content.title: Current status, evidence maturity, and translational readiness of artificial intelligence in dentistry: a bibliometric and thematic analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly expanded across dental research, particularly in imaging-based diagnostics and digital workflows. Despite the accelerating publication growth, the structural evolution, thematic maturity, and translational readiness of AI in dentistry remain insufficiently synthesised.

Methods

Publications related to AI in dentistry between 2015 and 2025 were retrieved from the Scopus database. Bibliometric analyses were conducted to examine annual outputs, countries, institutions, authors, journals, and keyword co-occurrence patterns. Network visualisation and clustering were performed using VOSviewer to identify research hotspots and thematic evolution. Selected evidence syntheses were evaluated using the Risk of Bias in Systematic Reviews (ROBIS) tool to assess methodological robustness and evidence maturity.

Results

A total of 3665 publications were included. Research output demonstrated marked post-2019 acceleration, with deep learning and convolutional neural networks dominating the methodological landscape.
